problem.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Twelve-year-old Greta spends her summer afternoons at her grandfather's allotment garden in Berlin.

All July, Herr Brandt and Frau Kessler argued about the fence between their plots: whether it stood ten centimeters too high, whether the club rules allowed it, whether it threw a shadow across Frau Kessler's beans. They measured it with folding rulers, wrote letters to the committee, and read the bylaws aloud to anyone who would listen. Meanwhile, a tomato plant that nobody had planted had pushed up through a crack in the roof of Herr Brandt's shed and now hung heavy with red fruit above both their heads. Greta watched the two neighbors stand beneath it for an hour, pointing at the fence, and neither once looked up. She began to suspect that what the adults actually cared about was ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Twelve-year-old Greta spends her summer afternoons at her grandfather's allotment garden in Berlin.

All July, Herr Brandt and Frau Kessler argued about the fence between their plots: whether it stood ten centimeters too high, whether the club rules allowed it, whether it threw a shadow across Frau Kessler's beans. They measured it with folding rulers, wrote letters to the committee, and read the bylaws aloud to anyone who would listen. Meanwhile, a tomato plant that nobody had planted had pushed up through a crack in the roof of Herr Brandt's shed and now hung heavy with red fruit above both their heads. Greta watched the two neighbors stand beneath it for an hour, pointing at the fence, and neither once looked up. She began to suspect that what the adults actually cared about was ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the dispute itself rather than anything the garden might actually produce.
the shade that the fence cast on Frau Kessler's crop of beans.
the unusual tomato plant, which they were secretly competing to claim.
the committee's rules, which they hoped to have rewritten that summer.
problem.explanation: 이웃들은 몇 시간씩 울타리 문제로 다투면서도 머리 위에 열매가 주렁주렁 달린 토마토는 한 번도 올려다보지 않는다. 이 두 사실을 함께 보면, 그들이 진짜 신경 쓰는 것은 정원의 수확이 아니라 다툼 그 자체라는 결론이 나오므로 A가 정답이다. B는 지문에 나온 콩의 그늘 문제를 가져왔지만, 콩을 정말 걱정하는 사람이 눈앞의 열매를 무시한다는 점과 맞지 않는다. C는 두 사람이 토마토를 전혀 보지 않았다는 서술과 모순된다. D는 규정을 읽는 행동에 근거하지만, 규정을 바꾸려 한다는 내용은 지문에 없고 그레타가 관찰한 대비도 설명하지 못한다.
problem.explanationEn: The neighbors argue about the fence for hours, yet neither one looks up at the tomato plant full of ripe fruit hanging right above them. When you put those two facts together, it's clear they care about the argument itself, not about anything the garden grows, so A is correct. B uses the detail about shade on the beans, but someone who truly cared about crops wouldn't ignore ripe fruit right over their head. C contradicts the text, which says neither neighbor ever looked up at the tomato. D builds on the neighbors reading the bylaws aloud, but the text never says they want the rules changed, and that idea doesn't explain the contrast Greta notices.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Twelve-year-old Greta notices that her Berlin allotment neighbors spend hours arguing about fence height while ignoring the tomato plant that has spontaneously grown through the shed roof.

hardJudge.note: 정답 A는 '울타리 논쟁에 몰두' + '머리 위 열매를 한 번도 보지 않음'이라는 두 정보를 연결해야 도출되는 추론으로 타당함. B(콩 그늘)와 D(규정 낭독)는 지문의 세부에 근거한 부분 정답형 오답이라 비교가 필요하고, C는 지문과 모순되지만 토마토를 언급해 그럴듯함. 지문은 원작 인용 흔적 없는 창작 각색으로 보임. 해설의 "몇 시간씩/for hours" 표현만 지문의 "an hour"와 미세하게 다름.

advisory.note: 울타리 다툼과 아무도 올려다보지 않은 토마토라는 두 단서를 연결해야 A가 나옴. B와 D는 지문 세부(콩 그늘, 규약 낭독)에 기대고 있어 그럴듯함. C는 비교적 쉽게 배제됨. 중간 난이도에 적합함.

problem.passage:
On the dock at Húsavík, the January wind came off the bay sharp enough to numb Bjorn's fingers through his gloves, so he worked bare-handed, as his father did. The torn net lay across his knees. His father had shown him the knot only once: loop, pass under, draw tight until the mesh square matched its neighbors exactly. Bjorn had tied hundreds that morning, quickly, pleased with his speed. Then his father lifted the section to the light, and water-heavy gaps sagged open wherever Bjorn had pulled a knot unevenly. "A cod finds the loose one," his father said, and handed the net back without another word. Bjorn untied every knot he had made. Working again, he counted each pass under his breath and measured each square against the one beside it before moving on. By dusk he had mended less than a third of what he had finished before noon, yet when he raised the net himself, he found that he ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: On the dock at Húsavík, the January wind came off the bay sharp enough to numb Bjorn's fingers through his gloves, so he worked bare-handed, as his father did. The torn net lay across his knees. His father had shown him the knot only once: loop, pass under, draw tight until the mesh square matched its neighbors exactly. Bjorn had tied hundreds that morning, quickly, pleased with his speed. Then his father lifted the section to the light, and water-heavy gaps sagged open wherever Bjorn had pulled a knot unevenly. "A cod finds the loose one," his father said, and handed the net back without another word. Bjorn untied every knot he had made. Working again, he counted each pass under his breath and measured each square against the one beside it before moving on. By dusk he had mended less than a third of what he had finished before noon, yet when he raised the net himself, he found that he ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: could finally tie the knots as fast as his father had tied them earlier that day
was looking for uneven squares with the same eye his father had turned on his morning's work
regretted throwing away his morning's work, since most of those knots had been sound
was now sure his father would praise how much of the net he had finished
problem.explanation: 비욘은 오전에 속도를 자랑했지만 아버지가 그물을 빛에 비춰 처진 틈을 찾아냈고, 이후 비욘은 칸 하나하나를 옆 칸과 비교하며 묶었습니다. 그래서 그가 직접 그물을 들어 올렸다는 것은 아버지처럼 고르지 않은 칸을 살펴보는 눈을 갖게 되었다는 뜻이므로 B가 정답입니다. A는 오후에 작업한 양이 오전의 3분의 1도 안 되었다는 내용과 맞지 않습니다. C는 매듭이 고르지 않아 틈이 벌어졌다는 내용과 모순됩니다. D는 아버지가 작업한 양이 아니라 정확성을 중시했다는 점을 놓쳤습니다.
problem.explanationEn: In the morning Bjorn was proud of how fast he worked, but his father held the net up to the light and found the gaps where knots were pulled unevenly. After that, Bjorn checked each square against the one next to it. So when he lifts the net himself, the logical conclusion is that he now inspects it the way his father did, which is choice B. Choice A doesn't fit, because he finished less than a third as much by dusk, so he hadn't gotten faster. Choice C contradicts the text, which says the morning's knots left gaps. Choice D misses the point that his father cared about precision, not how much got done.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Bjorn, a fishing boat captain's son, learns to mend nets on an Icelandic winter dock, each knot requiring a precision that exposes his previous carelessness.

hardJudge.note: 정답 B는 '아버지가 그물을 빛에 비춰 살핌' → '비욘이 직접 그물을 들어 올림'이라는 두 장면의 연결과 'yet'의 대조(양은 줄었으나 눈을 얻음)를 읽어야 도출되어 medium에 적합. A·D는 '3분의 1도 못 미침'으로 배제되고, C는 지문의 분위기·결과와 어긋남. 다만 A는 '아버지가 그날 매듭을 묶었다'는 전제 자체가 지문에 없어 다소 약한 오답. 창작 지문으로 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: B는 아버지가 그물을 빛에 비춰 살핀 장면과 비욘이 칸마다 옆 칸과 비교한 장면을 연결해야 고를 수 있으므로 타당한 추론입니다. A와 D는 비교적 쉽게 배제되고, C는 그럴듯한 오답입니다. medium 난이도의 하한선 수준입니다.

problem.passage:
The following is adapted from a scene in a 1950s novel set in Paris.

On the last Thursday of October 1952, Monsieur Aubert, who had come into Lucien Ferrand's bookshop every week for eleven years, set a parcel on the counter and left without his usual remark about the weather. Inside was a copy of Montaigne's Essays, its spine cracked, its corners soft as felt, a coffee ring blooming across the title page. Lucien turned it over twice. To give a bookseller a ruined book, he thought, was to tell him that his trade was worth nothing more than this. He slid the volume beneath the counter and did not look at it again that day.

Discussing this scene, literary scholar Hélène Marchetti argues that the novel invites readers to see what Lucien cannot: that the book's battered condition is itself the message, evidence of a devotion that Aubert built over many years and connected directly to Lucien.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Marchetti's argument?
problem.stimulus:
The following is adapted from a scene in a 1950s novel set in Paris.

On the last Thursday of October 1952, Monsieur Aubert, who had come into Lucien Ferrand's bookshop every week for eleven years, set a parcel on the counter and left without his usual remark about the weather. Inside was a copy of Montaigne's Essays, its spine cracked, its corners soft as felt, a coffee ring blooming across the title page. Lucien turned it over twice. To give a bookseller a ruined book, he thought, was to tell him that his trade was worth nothing more than this. He slid the volume beneath the counter and did not look at it again that day.

Discussing this scene, literary scholar Hélène Marchetti argues that the novel invites readers to see what Lucien cannot: that the book's battered condition is itself the message, evidence of a devotion that Aubert built over many years and connected directly to Lucien.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Marchetti's argument?
options: In a later chapter, Lucien realizes he misjudged Aubert and visits his apartment to say sorry, but finds that Aubert has moved away from Paris.
In a later chapter, Lucien remembers that his own father, also a bookseller, believed that no customer should ever give a used book as a gift.
In a later chapter, Lucien learns that Aubert first bought the volume at a different shop across the Seine before he started visiting Lucien's store.
In a later chapter, Lucien opens the volume and finds Aubert's dated notes in its margins, many responding to passages Lucien had recommended to him over the years.
problem.explanation: Marchetti의 주장에는 두 부분이 있다. 책이 낡은 것은 Aubert가 오랜 세월 쌓아 온 헌신의 증거라는 점, 그리고 그 헌신이 Lucien과 직접 이어져 있다는 점이다. D는 여러 해에 걸쳐 날짜가 적힌 메모(오랜 반복 독서)를 보여 주고, 그 메모가 Lucien이 추천한 구절에 대한 응답(Lucien과의 연결)임을 보여 주므로 두 조건을 모두 충족한다. A는 Lucien이 자신의 오해를 깨닫는다는 내용이지만, 책의 상태가 무엇을 뜻하는지는 설명하지 못한다. B는 오히려 선물을 모욕으로 본 Lucien의 해석에 배경을 줄 뿐이다. C는 책의 내력을 알려 주지만 Lucien과 무관한 곳에서 산 책이므로 헌신이 Lucien과 연결된다는 점을 뒷받침하지 못한다.
problem.explanationEn: Marchetti's argument has two parts: the book's worn condition is evidence of devotion Aubert built up over many years, and that devotion is tied directly to Lucien. D satisfies both. Notes dated across many years show long, repeated reading, and the fact that they respond to passages Lucien recommended links the wear to Lucien himself. A shows that Lucien realizes he was wrong, but it says nothing about what the book's condition means. B only gives background for Lucien's view that the gift was an insult. C tells you where the book came from, but because Aubert bought it somewhere unrelated to Lucien, it actually fails to connect the book to him.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A Parisian bookseller in 1952 misinterprets a regular customer's gift of a worn volume, believing it an insult rather than an act of devotion.

hardJudge.note: Marchetti의 주장은 (1) 낡은 상태 = 오랜 헌신의 증거, (2) 그 헌신이 Lucien과 직접 연결, 두 조건으로 구성됨. D만이 두 조건을 모두 충족(여러 해에 걸친 날짜 메모 + Lucien 추천 구절에 대한 응답). A는 '오해 깨달음'이라는 부분적 근거가 있으나 책 상태의 의미를 설명하지 못하고, C는 책의 내력(오랜 소유)을 주지만 Lucien과의 연결을 끊음. B는 Lucien의 해석을 뒷받침하는 쪽. 오답 2개가 부분적 근거를 가지므로 medium에 적합. 한국어·영어 해설 결론 및 선택지 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 가상 소설 발췌로 저작권 우려 없음.

advisory.note: 두 조건(오랜 헌신 + Lucien과의 연결)을 모두 확인해야 하는 구조임. A와 C는 일부 근거만 갖춘 오답이어서 medium 난이도에 맞음. 정답 D가 유일하게 두 조건을 모두 충족함.

problem.passage:
Text 1
In Margarethe Lind's novel The Fourth Zone, the boarder Frau Keller spends three days crossing postwar Vienna to recover a single letter left at her old address. Critics usually praise how closely Lind shows the city split among four occupying powers: the checkpoints, the ruined tram lines, the guards' changing languages. That divided city is the book's real subject. The letter itself is little more than a pretext, a device that keeps Keller moving so that readers can see Vienna's divisions.

Text 2
No reader can forget Lind's checkpoints, and they have earned their praise. But the city takes its shape from Keller's errand. At each barrier she silently repeats the name of her brother, who wrote the letter, and she judges every delay by how much it postpones the moment she will hold his words. The British sector feels hostile to her not because of its soldiers but because its detours cost her an afternoon. Take away the letter and Lind's Vienna loses the urgency that makes it vivid.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the claim in Text 1 about the role of the letter in Lind's novel?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
In Margarethe Lind's novel The Fourth Zone, the boarder Frau Keller spends three days crossing postwar Vienna to recover a single letter left at her old address. Critics usually praise how closely Lind shows the city split among four occupying powers: the checkpoints, the ruined tram lines, the guards' changing languages. That divided city is the book's real subject. The letter itself is little more than a pretext, a device that keeps Keller moving so that readers can see Vienna's divisions.

Text 2
No reader can forget Lind's checkpoints, and they have earned their praise. But the city takes its shape from Keller's errand. At each barrier she silently repeats the name of her brother, who wrote the letter, and she judges every delay by how much it postpones the moment she will hold his words. The British sector feels hostile to her not because of its soldiers but because its detours cost her an afternoon. Take away the letter and Lind's Vienna loses the urgency that makes it vivid.
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the claim in Text 1 about the role of the letter in Lind's novel?
options: By agreeing that the divided city is powerfully portrayed while maintaining that Keller's attachment to the letter governs how that city is experienced
By agreeing that the letter is incidental to the plot while maintaining that Keller's brother is the novel's true central concern
By disputing that the city is powerfully portrayed while maintaining that the checkpoints are less memorable than critics suggest
By disputing that Keller ever reaches the letter while maintaining that her journey is ultimately left unfinished
problem.explanation: Text 2의 저자는 검문소 묘사가 칭찬받을 만하다고 인정하면서도("No reader can forget... earned their praise"), 도시가 편지라는 용무를 통해 형태를 갖는다고 주장한다. 따라서 편지가 단순한 구실이라는 Text 1의 주장을 반박하고, 편지가 도시 경험을 좌우한다고 볼 것이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 오빠를 중요하게 본다는 점은 맞지만, 편지가 부수적이라는 데 동의한다는 부분이 Text 2의 핵심 주장과 반대된다. C는 Text 2가 도시 묘사를 칭찬하므로 틀렸다. D는 Text 2에 Keller가 편지를 찾는지에 대한 언급이 없으므로 근거가 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The author of Text 2 grants that Lind's checkpoints "have earned their praise," but argues that the city "takes its shape from Keller's errand," meaning that the letter controls how she experiences each delay and sector. So this author would accept Text 1's praise of the divided city while rejecting the idea that the letter is a mere pretext, which is choice A. Choice B is partly right because the brother does matter in Text 2, but it says the author agrees the letter is incidental, and Text 2 argues the opposite. Choice C is wrong because Text 2 praises the city's portrayal rather than questioning it. Choice D has no support, since neither text discusses whether Keller actually gets the letter.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Frau Keller, a postwar Vienna boarder, takes a three-day journey across the fractured city to retrieve a single letter she fears may have been lost forever.

hardJudge.note: Text 2 explicitly concedes the checkpoints "have earned their praise" and then argues the city "takes its shape from Keller's errand," directly contradicting Text 1's "pretext" claim—A is the only choice capturing both the concession and the rebuttal. B is a strong partial-credit distractor (brother does matter, but "letter is incidental" reverses Text 2's thesis); C inverts the concession; D is unsupported but surface-plausible. Korean and English explanations match in conclusion and letter references, with no Hangul in the English version. Fictional novel/author, no copyright concern. Two-step reasoning (identify concession + identify counterclaim) suits medium.

advisory.note: 정답 A는 타당하다. 그러나 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가진 오답은 B 하나뿐이다. C는 Text 2 첫 문장("earned their praise")과 정면으로 모순되고, D는 두 지문 어디에도 근거가 없어 훑어 읽어도 바로 걸러진다. 'medium' 기준인 '오답 3개 중 최소 2개가 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가질 것'을 충족하지 못한다.

problem.passage:
On the last morning of the term, Teacher Mateo did not speak of sheep. He stood at the window of the one-room schoolhouse, where the wind off the Patagonian steppe rattled the tin roof like loose coins, and pointed upward at the wide, colorless sky that the ranch children had long ago stopped noticing ______ it was, he told them quietly, the only thing on the estancia that no one would ever own.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: On the last morning of the term, Teacher Mateo did not speak of sheep. He stood at the window of the one-room schoolhouse, where the wind off the Patagonian steppe rattled the tin roof like loose coins, and pointed upward at the wide, colorless sky that the ranch children had long ago stopped noticing ______ it was, he told them quietly, the only thing on the estancia that no one would ever own.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: and,
(no punctuation)
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "He stood ... noticing"은 긴 관계절과 수식어가 붙어 있지만 하나의 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "it was ... own"도 주어와 동사를 가진 독립절이다. 두 독립절을 연결하려면 세미콜론이 필요하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 뒤에 나오는 삽입구 "he told them" 주변의 쉼표들과 비슷해 보이지만, 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이으면 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 된다. B는 접속사 and를 쓴 점은 맞지만, 쉼표를 and 앞이 아니라 뒤에 두어 문장부호 위치가 잘못되었다. D는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다.
problem.explanationEn: The words before the blank, "He stood ... noticing," make up one independent clause, even though long relative clauses and modifiers are attached to it. The words after the blank, "it was ... own," form a second independent clause with its own subject and verb. To join two independent clauses, you need a semicolon, so C is correct. A might look right because it matches the commas around "he told them," but a comma alone between two independent clauses is a comma splice. B correctly uses the conjunction "and," but the comma goes after "and" instead of before it, so the punctuation is in the wrong place. D puts no punctuation between the clauses at all, which makes a run-on sentence.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Teacher Mateo delivers his final lesson to ranch children on the Patagonian steppe, speaking not of sheep but of the sky they are learning to ignore.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞 "He stood ... stopped noticing"은 관계절·수식어가 길게 붙은 하나의 독립절이고, 뒤 "it was ... own"도 독립절이므로 세미콜론(C)이 유일한 정답. A는 comma splice, B는 and 뒤 쉼표로 위치 오류, D는 run-on(단, "noticing it was..."가 명사절처럼 읽혀 유혹적임). 긴 문장 구조에서 절 경계를 찾아야 하고 A·D가 부분적 근거를 가지므로 medium에 적합. 한·영 해설 모두 정답 및 선택지 참조가 일치하고 오류 없음.

advisory.note: 관계절이 길어 절의 경계가 가려지고, 뒤 절의 삽입구 쉼표가 A를 그럴듯하게 만든다. 그래서 중간 난이도에 대체로 맞는다. 다만 B와 D는 비교적 쉽게 배제된다.

problem.passage:
For eleven years, Carlos and Eduardo had refused to share so much as a thermos of coffee at the San Isidro depot. But on the night a rockslide trapped both of their buses on the switchbacks above the village, Eduardo, the driver who had once reported Carlos for leaving three minutes early, did something no one at the depot would have predicted ______ walked down the dark road to Carlos's stalled bus, a coil of tow rope over his shoulder, and asked where to tie it.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: For eleven years, Carlos and Eduardo had refused to share so much as a thermos of coffee at the San Isidro depot. But on the night a rockslide trapped both of their buses on the switchbacks above the village, Eduardo, the driver who had once reported Carlos for leaving three minutes early, did something no one at the depot would have predicted ______ walked down the dark road to Carlos's stalled bus, a coil of tow rope over his shoulder, and asked where to tie it.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , he
; and he
he
: he
problem.explanation: 긴 동격구(the driver who...)를 걷어내면 'Eduardo did something no one would have predicted'가 완전한 독립절이고, 뒤의 'he walked...'도 독립절이며 그 '예측 못 한 일'을 구체적으로 설명한다. 앞 절이 완결되고 뒤 절이 그 내용을 풀어 설명하므로 콜론을 쓰는 D가 정답이다. A는 독립절 두 개를 쉼표만으로 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. B는 세미콜론 뒤에 등위접속사 and를 붙여 쓴 비표준 형태이다. C는 두 독립절을 아무 문장부호 없이 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다.
problem.explanationEn: If you set aside the long appositive (the driver who...), "Eduardo did something no one at the depot would have predicted" is a complete independent clause. "He walked..." is also an independent clause, and it spells out what that unexpected act was. A colon is the right mark when a complete clause is followed by an explanation of it, so D is correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B puts the conjunction "and" after a semicolon, which is not standard. C runs the two clauses together with no punctuation at all.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Two rival bus drivers at a Mexican mountain depot—Carlos and Eduardo—develop grudging respect after a shared crisis forces them to help one another.

hardJudge.note: 검산: 'Eduardo ... did something no one at the depot would have predicted'는 완전한 독립절, 'he walked ... and asked ...'도 독립절이며 앞 절의 '예측 못 한 일'을 구체화하므로 콜론(D)이 적절. A는 comma splice, B는 세미콜론+and 비표준, C는 run-on. 긴 삽입 동격구와 부사절이 주절 경계 파악을 요구해 두 단계 판단이 필요하며, A·B가 부분적 타당성을 갖는 오답으로 기능하므로 medium 적합. 한·영 해설 결론 및 선택지 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음.

advisory.note: 긴 동격구 때문에 주절의 구조를 다시 파악해야 하고, 그다음 콜론의 설명 기능을 확인해야 하는 두 단계 판단이 필요해 medium 난이도에 맞다. B(세미콜론+and)를 비표준으로 본 해설은 엄밀히 따지면 논란의 여지가 있지만 SAT 관례에는 부합한다. 다만 뒤 절이 앞 절을 구체화한다는 점에서 콜론이 가장 적절하다는 근거를 덧붙이면 더 좋겠다.

problem.passage:
Every morning the school boat left Tagbac before the tide turned, and the children, crowded beneath its patched blue canopy, made up games to fill the hour. The newest game, invented by Lorna Dimaculangan, a quiet girl who swore she had dreamed it during the last typhoon______ that anyone walking between the island's villages at midday must never once step on his or her own shadow. By the time the boat reached the pier, even the boatman was squinting at the sun and planning his route home.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Every morning the school boat left Tagbac before the tide turned, and the children, crowded beneath its patched blue canopy, made up games to fill the hour. The newest game, invented by Lorna Dimaculangan, a quiet girl who swore she had dreamed it during the last typhoon______ that anyone walking between the island's villages at midday must never once step on his or her own shadow. By the time the boat reached the pier, even the boatman was squinting at the sun and planning his route home.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , required
required
; required
—required
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "The newest game"이고 동사는 "required"이다. 그 사이에 "invented by ..."라는 수식어와 "a quiet girl who ... typhoon"이라는 동격구가 끼어 있다. 동격구가 쉼표로 시작했으므로 같은 쉼표로 닫아야 하고, 그래서 A가 정답이다. B는 닫는 쉼표가 없어서 "typhoon required"가 관계절 속 동사처럼 읽혀 버린다. C의 세미콜론은 주어와 동사를 갈라놓아 앞부분이 독립절이 되지 못한다. D의 대시는 쉼표로 연 삽입구를 다른 부호로 닫는 것이라 짝이 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is "The newest game," and its verb is "required." Between them sit the modifier "invented by ..." and the appositive "a quiet girl who ... typhoon." That appositive opens with a comma, so it has to close with a comma too, and that makes A correct. B leaves out the closing comma, so "typhoon required" reads as if the verb belonged inside the "who" clause. C puts a semicolon between the subject and its verb, and that's a problem because the words before a semicolon must form an independent clause, which they don't here. D closes with a dash even though the interruption opened with a comma, so the punctuation doesn't match.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On a Philippine island school boat, children invent a game where neighbors must navigate between villages without stepping on their own shadow.

hardJudge.note: 주어 "The newest game"과 동사 "required" 사이에 긴 삽입 수식어(분사구 + 동격구 + 관계절)가 끼어 있고, 삽입은 쉼표로 열렸으므로 쉼표로 닫는 A가 유일한 정답. B는 닫는 부호 누락, C는 세미콜론 앞이 독립절이 아님, D는 여는 부호(쉼표)와 닫는 부호(대시)가 불일치. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 같은 결론과 글자 참조를 가지며 정확하고 자연스러움. 긴 삽입구 속 중첩 구조를 추적해야 하므로 medium에 적합. 지문은 창작 원문으로 저작권 우려 없음.

advisory.note: 주어-동사 사이에 긴 삽입구(분사구+동격구+관계절)가 있어 짝 쉼표를 찾아야 하는 2단계 판단이 필요하다. 표준 medium 수준이다. 엄밀히 보면 삽입 요소는 'invented' 앞의 쉼표로 열리지만, 해설이 동격구 기준으로 설명해도 결론은 같다.

The name on the front, a Mrs. Wanjiru Kamau of Ngong Road, belonged to a woman Priya had never heard of______ the return address, written in a careful, slanting hand, gave a street in Kampala. Later that week, a clerk at the post office told her that Mrs. Kamau had long since moved to Lusaka.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Priya found the envelope wedged beneath a torn seat on the matatu to Westlands, its stamp faded to the color of weak tea and its postmark dated 1994. The name on the front, a Mrs. Wanjiru Kamau of Ngong Road, belonged to a woman Priya had never heard of______ the return address, written in a careful, slanting hand, gave a street in Kampala. Later that week, a clerk at the post office told her that Mrs. Kamau had long since moved to Lusaka.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , the
; the
the
, and, the
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "The name on the front, ... belonged to a woman Priya had never heard of"는 삽입된 동격구가 있어도 완전한 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "the return address ... gave a street in Kampala"도 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. C는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 run-on 문장이다. D는 등위접속사 and를 쓴 점은 맞지만 and 뒤에 쉼표를 두어 접속사와 이어지는 절을 불필요하게 갈라놓는다.
problem.explanationEn: The part before the blank, "The name on the front, ... belonged to a woman Priya had never heard of," is a complete independent clause even with the appositive in the middle, and the part after it, "the return address ... gave a street in Kampala," is also an independent clause. A semicolon can join two independent clauses, so B is correct. A connects the two clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C puts no punctuation between the clauses, which creates a run-on sentence. D is right to use the conjunction "and," but the comma after "and" wrongly separates the conjunction from the clause it introduces.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Priya finds a letter on the Nairobi matatu that arrived thirty years too late, addressed to someone who now lives three countries away.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞뒤 모두 독립절(앞 절은 동격구 삽입, 뒤 절은 분사구 삽입으로 구조 파악에 한 단계 더 필요). 세미콜론(B)만 적법. A는 comma splice, C는 fused sentence, D는 "and" 뒤 불필요한 쉼표. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 B를 일관되게 뒷받침하며 글자 참조 일치. 삽입구 때문에 절 경계를 정독해야 하고 A·D가 부분적으로 타당해 보여 medium에 부합. 창작 지문으로 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: Standard comma splice/semicolon item. The appositive adds a bit of distraction, and D is a plausible distractor, so the medium level fits. It may lean slightly easy because C is clearly wrong.

problem.passage:
Jin and Sora had surfaced side by side for forty years, their breath-whistles rising together over the cold swells off Jeju. Now, as Sora coiled her rope on the black rocks and talked about her aching knees, about her granddaughter in Seoul, about the blue gate she would finally have time to repaint______ said nothing, and for the first time the silence between them felt less like comfort than like a door being slowly closed.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Jin and Sora had surfaced side by side for forty years, their breath-whistles rising together over the cold swells off Jeju. Now, as Sora coiled her rope on the black rocks and talked about her aching knees, about her granddaughter in Seoul, about the blue gate she would finally have time to repaint______ said nothing, and for the first time the silence between them felt less like comfort than like a door being slowly closed.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: ; Jin
: Jin
, Jin
, and Jin
problem.explanation: 'as Sora coiled... repaint'는 'as'로 시작하는 종속절이고, 주절은 'Jin said nothing'입니다. 도입 종속절과 주절 사이에는 쉼표 하나를 쓰므로 C가 정답입니다. A의 세미콜론은 앞뒤가 모두 독립절일 때만 쓸 수 있는데, 앞부분은 길어도 종속절이라 혼자 문장이 될 수 없습니다. B의 콜론도 앞에 완전한 독립절이 있어야 하므로 같은 이유로 틀립니다. D는 쉼표+and로 종속절을 주절과 대등하게 연결해 버려서, 'as' 절이 수식할 주절이 사라집니다.
problem.explanationEn: The part starting with "as Sora coiled... repaint" is a dependent clause, and the main clause is "Jin said nothing." When an introductory dependent clause comes before the main clause, you separate them with a single comma, so C is correct. A doesn't work because a semicolon has to join two independent clauses, and even though the opening is long, it's a dependent clause that can't stand alone. B fails for the same reason, since a colon needs a complete independent clause before it. D adds "and," which links the dependent clause to the main clause as if they were equal, so the "as" clause no longer has a main clause to modify.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Divers Jin and Sora have been haenyeo partners for forty years, but as one plans to retire, their comfortable silence begins to feel like goodbye.

hardJudge.note: 'Now, as Sora coiled ... repaint' is a long introductory subordinate clause (with an internal 'about...' series that invites misreading it as independent); the main clause is 'Jin said nothing'. Only a comma (C) correctly separates them. A and B require an independent clause before the mark; D's ', and' leaves the 'as' clause with no main clause. Both explanations match the answer and letter references and are accurate; English is natural with no Hangul. Two-step judgment (identify clause type despite length/internal commas, then apply punctuation rule) suits medium.

advisory.note: 'Now, as ... repaint'라는 긴 종속절이 있고, 그 안에 about 병렬 구문이 들어가 있어서 종속절이 어디서 끝나는지 파악하기 어렵습니다. 그래서 훑어 읽으면 세미콜론이나 콜론을 고르는 오답을 유도하므로 medium 난이도에 적합합니다. D도 'and'가 있으니 그럴듯해 보이는 오답입니다.

When his brother Tobias finally came up to the pilothouse, Elias pushed the folded sheet across the wheel without a word. Tobias, who had not spoken to him since their father's funeral and who had boarded the boat only because no other passage south was ______ the map open slowly, as if it might tear.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Captain Elias Merrow had spent three nights at the chart table drawing the river from Cairo to Natchez, marking every sandbar and snag he had learned in twenty years of piloting. When his brother Tobias finally came up to the pilothouse, Elias pushed the folded sheet across the wheel without a word. Tobias, who had not spoken to him since their father's funeral and who had boarded the boat only because no other passage south was ______ the map open slowly, as if it might tear.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: available; unfolded
available, and unfolded
available unfolded
available, unfolded
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 Tobias이고 본동사는 unfolded이며, 그 사이의 'who had not spoken... available'은 앞쪽 쉼표로 열린 비필수 관계절이다. 따라서 이 삽입절을 닫는 쉼표 하나가 필요하므로 D가 정답이다. A의 세미콜론은 앞뒤에 독립절이 있어야 하는데, 앞부분은 주어만 있고 동사가 없는 불완전한 절이다. B의 'and'는 unfolded를 관계절 속 동사(had boarded)와 나란히 묶어 버려 주어 Tobias에게 본동사가 남지 않는다. C는 삽입절을 닫는 쉼표가 빠져 있어 'available unfolded'가 잘못 붙어 읽힌다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is Tobias and its main verb is unfolded. Between them sits a nonessential relative clause ("who had not spoken... available") that opens with a comma, so it needs a matching comma to close it, which makes D correct. A uses a semicolon, but a semicolon needs an independent clause on each side, and the part before it has a subject with no main verb. B adds "and," which pairs unfolded with the verb inside the relative clause (had boarded), so Tobias ends up with no main verb. C leaves out the closing comma, so the clause never ends and "available unfolded" runs together.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On a nineteenth-century riverboat, a steamboat captain gives his estranged brother a hand-drawn map, a gesture neither can quite articulate.

hardJudge.note: 검산: 주어 Tobias + 쉼표로 열린 비필수 관계절(who... and who... available) + 본동사 unfolded 구조이므로 닫는 쉼표가 필요한 D가 유일하게 옳음. A는 세미콜론 앞이 독립절이 아님, B는 'and'가 본동사를 관계절에 흡수시켜 주절 동사 소실, C는 닫는 쉼표 누락. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 동일 결론·글자 참조로 정확하며 자연스러움. 긴 삽입절과 두 개의 who절을 추적해야 하므로 medium에 적합. 원창작 지문으로 저작권 우려 없음.

advisory.note: 긴 비필수 관계절 안에 다시 'who ... and who' 병렬 구조가 들어 있다. 그래서 수험생은 주어-동사를 찾은 뒤 삽입절을 닫는 쉼표가 필요하다는 것까지 두 단계로 판단해야 한다. B는 관계절 안의 병렬 구조 때문에 그럴듯하게 보이는 매력적인 오답이다. medium 난이도에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
Amara had assumed the stranger sharing the narrow ledge beneath the rooftop water tank was just another office clerk caught by the monsoon without an umbrella. But when Dev mentioned the salt-stung cashew groves and the crooked lighthouse at the edge of his childhood town, a place neither of them had returned to in more than a decade______ realized that they had once lived only a few lanes apart.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Amara had assumed the stranger sharing the narrow ledge beneath the rooftop water tank was just another office clerk caught by the monsoon without an umbrella. But when Dev mentioned the salt-stung cashew groves and the crooked lighthouse at the edge of his childhood town, a place neither of them had returned to in more than a decade______ realized that they had once lived only a few lanes apart.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , she
; she
, and she
. She
problem.explanation: 이 문장은 "when"으로 시작하는 종속절이 "a place ... decade"라는 긴 동격어구로 끝나고, 그 뒤에 주절 "she realized..."가 온다. 문장 앞에 오는 종속절과 주절은 쉼표로 연결하므로 A가 정답이다. B의 세미콜론은 앞뒤가 모두 독립절이어야 쓸 수 있는데, 앞부분은 "when" 때문에 종속절이다. C의 ", and"도 앞부분을 독립절로 잘못 본 것이다. 종속절에 주절을 등위접속사로 이을 수는 없다. D는 앞부분을 "But when..."으로 시작하는 문장 조각(fragment)으로 남긴다.
problem.explanationEn: The sentence opens with a dependent clause beginning with "when," and that clause ends with a long appositive ("a place ... decade"). After it comes the main clause "she realized...." A comma is the standard way to join an introductory dependent clause to a main clause, so A is correct. B uses a semicolon, which needs an independent clause on both sides, but "when" makes the first part dependent. C uses ", and," which also wrongly treats the first part as an independent clause, and a coordinating conjunction can't join a dependent clause to a main clause. D leaves "But when..." standing alone as a sentence fragment.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Amara and Dev, strangers sheltering from monsoon rain on a Mumbai rooftop, discover they both fled the same coastal town years ago.

hardJudge.note: 검산: "But when Dev mentioned ... town, a place ... decade" 전체가 when 종속절(동격어구 포함)이고 주절은 "she realized..."이므로 쉼표(A)가 유일한 정답. B(세미콜론)·C(, and)는 앞부분을 독립절로 오인한 것이고 D는 조각문을 만든다. 긴 동격어구가 구조를 가려 훑어 읽으면 B/C에 끌리도록 설계되어 medium에 적합. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답과 선택지 글자 참조가 일치하고 오류 없음.

advisory.note: 긴 동격어구 때문에 종속절 경계를 찾기 어려워 medium 수준에 맞음. 오답 B, C, D 모두 그럴듯함.

, meanwhile
; meanwhile
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "It belonged ... since 1945"는 긴 동격구로 끝나는 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "he slept ..."도 독립절이다. 두 독립절을 접속부사 meanwhile로 이으려면 앞에 세미콜론, 뒤에 쉼표를 써야 하므로 B가 정답이다. A와 C는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다(meanwhile은 등위접속사가 아니다). D는 세미콜론은 맞지만 문장 앞머리 접속부사 meanwhile 뒤에 쉼표가 빠져 있다.
problem.explanationEn: The part before the blank, "It belonged ... since 1945," is an independent clause, even though it ends with a long appositive. The part after the blank, "he slept ...," is also an independent clause. If you join two independent clauses with the conjunctive adverb "meanwhile," you need a semicolon before it and a comma after it, so B is correct. A and C use only a comma to join the two clauses, which makes a comma splice, because "meanwhile" is not a coordinating conjunction. D has the correct semicolon, but it leaves out the comma that should follow "meanwhile" at the start of the clause.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Rolf, a postwar Vienna boarder, must decide whether to remain in the comfortable, cramped room he shares or reclaim the family apartment standing empty.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞뒤 모두 독립절이므로 세미콜론+접속부사+쉼표(B)가 표준 정답이며, A·C는 comma splice로 명확히 배제된다. 다만 B와 D의 유일한 차이가 접속부사 meanwhile 뒤 쉼표 유무인데, 이는 실제 용법에서 선택적(특히 짧은 부사)으로 취급되는 경우가 많아 D를 '오류'로 단정하기 약하다. 실제 디지털 SAT는 세미콜론 뒤 접속부사의 쉼표 유무만으로 정오를 가르는 설계를 피하는 경향이 있으므로, 변별 근거의 견고성 측면에서 주의가 필요하다(판정 범위 내에서는 B가 최선의 선택임은 인정). 긴 동격구 뒤에 절 경계를 숨긴 점은 medium 난이도에 부합.

advisory.note: 세미콜론 + 접속부사 + 쉼표를 묻는 표준 문항이다. 앞 독립절이 긴 동격구로 끝나서 절 경계를 찾기가 조금 어려워지고, 이 점이 medium 난이도에 맞다. D는 SAT 관례상 오답으로 처리하는 전형적인 선택지다.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Marcus had been counting the cars of the approaching Ravenswood train when he saw it. The man beside him on the elevated platform, a tall figure in a gray overcoat who had been checking his wristwatch every few seconds______ the gold band from his finger and let it slip into his coat pocket. No one else on the crowded platform seemed to notice.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: ; twisted
— twisted
, twisted
twisted
problem.explanation: 주어 "The man beside him on the elevated platform" 뒤에 쉼표로 시작하는 동격어구(a tall figure ... every few seconds)가 삽입되어 있고, 그 뒤에 본동사 twisted가 온다. 쉼표로 열린 비필수 삽입구는 쉼표로 닫아야 하므로 C가 정답이다. A의 세미콜론은 주어와 동사를 끊어 앞부분을 독립절이 아닌 조각으로 만든다. B의 대시는 삽입구를 닫는 데 쓸 수 있지만 쉼표로 연 삽입구를 대시로 닫으면 부호가 일치하지 않는다. D는 닫는 부호가 없어서 seconds twisted가 한 덩어리처럼 읽히고, 삽입구가 어디서 끝나는지 알 수 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject, "The man beside him on the elevated platform," is followed by an appositive that opens with a comma ("a tall figure ... every few seconds"), and then the main verb "twisted" comes next. A nonessential phrase that opens with a comma has to close with a comma, so C is correct. A uses a semicolon, which cuts the subject off from its verb and leaves a fragment before the semicolon. B uses a dash, which can close an interruption, but only when a dash opened it; closing a comma-opened phrase with a dash mixes the punctuation. D has no closing punctuation, so "seconds twisted" runs together and the reader can't tell where the appositive ends.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On a 1960s Chicago elevated platform, ten-year-old Marcus watches a man slip a wedding ring into his coat pocket, a gesture no one else seems to notice.

hardJudge.note: 주어 "The man beside him on the elevated platform" 뒤에 쉼표로 열린 동격 삽입구가 "every few seconds"까지 이어지고 본동사 twisted가 뒤따르므로 쉼표로 닫는 C가 유일하게 옳다. A(세미콜론)는 주어와 동사를 분리해 조각을 만들고, B(대시)는 쉼표로 연 삽입구와 부호가 불일치하며, D는 경계가 사라진다. 해설(한·영) 결론과 글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 삽입구 시작점을 역추적해 부호 짝을 맞추는 두 단계 판단이 필요하고 B·A가 부분적 타당성을 가져 medium 적합. 지문은 창작물로 저작권 문제 없음. D 선택지의 공백 두 칸은 사소한 표기 차이.

advisory.note: 동격어구 안에 관계절(who had been checking...)이 길게 들어 있어서 동사 twisted를 찾으려면 앞뒤를 연결해 읽어야 하므로 중간 난이도에 맞는다. B와 D는 부분적으로 그럴듯한 오답이다. D 선택지 앞에 공백이 두 칸 들어간 것은 사소한 표기 문제다.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Every weekday at 7:40, the Johnsons climbed to the Garfield Boulevard platform in the same order: Mr. Johnson first, then his wife, then nine-year-old Della with her lunch pail. But on the cold Tuesday that a gaunt brown dog appeared beneath the platform bench, ribs showing through its matted coat, Della knelt beside it and would not move. As the southbound train rattled in and out without them, the routine of the household, built over years of punctual departures and carefully pressed shirts, ______ apart in a single stubborn refusal to stand up.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: were coming
having come
to come
came
problem.explanation: 이 절의 주어는 단수 명사 'the routine'이고, 삽입된 수식어구 'built over years of ... shirts' 다음에 정동사가 와야 절이 완성된다. D의 'came'은 단수 주어와 맞는 정동사이며, 앞 문장들의 과거 시제와도 일치한다. A의 'were coming'은 정동사이긴 하지만 수식어구 안의 복수 명사(departures, shirts)에 맞춘 복수형이라 단수 주어 'routine'과 일치하지 않는다. B의 'having come'과 C의 'to come'은 비정형(분사·부정사)이어서 주어 'routine'에 정동사가 없게 되므로 문장이 성립하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this clause is the singular noun "the routine," and after the modifier "built over years of ... shirts," the clause still needs a main verb to be complete. Choice D, "came," is a main verb that agrees with the singular subject and also fits the past tense used in the rest of the passage. Choice A, "were coming," is a main verb, but it's plural: it agrees with the nouns inside the modifier ("departures," "shirts"), not with the singular subject "routine." Choices B ("having come") and C ("to come") are nonfinite forms (a participle and an infinitive), so "routine" would be left with no main verb and the sentence wouldn't work.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — The Johnsons' orderly 1960s Chicago household transforms when a half-starved dog appears on their elevated train platform and their daughter refuses to leave it.

hardJudge.note: 주어 'the routine of the household'(단수) 뒤에 긴 분사 수식어구 'built over years of punctual departures and carefully pressed shirts'가 삽입되어 있으며, 빈칸에는 정동사가 필요하다. D 'came'은 단수·과거 정동사로 정답이 맞다. A는 수식어구 내 복수 명사에 이끌린 수 일치 오류, B·C는 비정형으로 문장이 성립하지 않는다. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 동일한 결론과 선택지 참조를 갖고 정확하다. 수식어구를 건너뛰어 주어를 찾는 단계와 정동사/비정형 판별 단계가 결합되어 있어 medium에 적합하다. 지문은 독창적으로 보이며 저작권 의심 없음.

advisory.note: 'household'의 주어는 단수 'routine'이고 그 뒤에 수식어구가 끼어 있다. 'came'은 정동사이자 과거 시제여서 옳다. A는 복수 명사에 끌린 수 일치 함정이고, B와 C는 비정형이라 정동사가 없어진다. 두 단계로 판단해야 해서 중간 난이도에 맞는다.

Clutching the small cedar box against his chest as the minibus lurched past the Kenyatta Avenue stage, ______ the conductor calling out destinations he had heard a thousand times before.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: Kamau barely heard
Kamau's ears barely caught
there was barely any notice by Kamau of
the words barely reached Kamau from
problem.explanation: 이 문장은 분사구 'Clutching the small cedar box…'로 시작하므로, 바로 뒤에 오는 주어가 상자를 움켜쥔 사람이어야 한다. A는 주어가 Kamau라서 수식 관계가 맞고, 뒤의 목적어 'the conductor calling out…'과도 자연스럽게 이어진다. B는 Kamau라는 이름이 들어 있어 맞아 보이지만, 실제 주어는 'Kamau's ears'여서 귀가 상자를 움켜쥔 꼴이 된다. C는 주어 자리에 허사 there가 있어 분사구가 꾸밀 대상이 없다. D는 주어가 'the words'라서 말이 상자를 움켜쥔 꼴이 된다.
problem.explanationEn: The sentence opens with the participial phrase "Clutching the small cedar box…," so the subject that comes right after it has to be the person holding the box. Choice A makes Kamau the subject, so the modifier attaches correctly, and the object "the conductor calling out…" follows naturally. Choice B looks right because it includes Kamau's name, but its actual subject is "Kamau's ears," which would mean his ears were clutching the box. Choice C puts the placeholder "there" in the subject position, so the opening phrase has nothing to modify. Choice D makes "the words" the subject, which would mean the words were clutching the box.

hardJudge.note: 분사구 'Clutching the small cedar box…'의 수식 대상이 주어여야 하므로 Kamau가 주어인 A만 정답. B('Kamau's ears'), C(허사 there), D('the words')는 모두 현수 분사 오류. B는 이름이 포함되어 훑어 읽으면 매력적인 오답이고 D도 의미상 그럴듯하여 비교가 필요하므로 medium 적합. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 선택지 글자 참조와 결론이 일치하며 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 독창적 서사로 저작권 우려 없음.

advisory.note: 현수 수식어 문항. B의 소유격 함정이 비교를 요구하고, D도 문법적으로는 성립해 보여 medium 수준에 맞음. C는 상대적으로 쉽게 배제됨.

problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: were teaching
taught
teaching
have taught
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "The rhythm"이고, 콤마 사이의 긴 분사구(pulling ... hull)는 삽입된 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 단수 주어와 맞으면서 지문의 과거 시제(spoke, did, came, could)와도 맞는 정동사가 필요하므로 B "taught"가 정답이다. A는 과거 시제는 맞지만 복수형이어서, 가까이 있는 "hands"나 "waves"에 잘못 맞춘 것이다. C는 분사라서 문장에 정동사가 없게 된다. D는 복수형인 데다 현재완료여서 서술 시제와도 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "The rhythm." The long phrase between the commas (pulling ... hull) only modifies it. So you need a main verb that is singular and also matches the passage's past tense (spoke, did, came, could). That makes B, "taught," the answer. A is in the past tense, but it's plural, so it wrongly agrees with nearby nouns like "hands" or "waves." C is a participle, which leaves the sentence without a main verb. D is plural and in the present perfect, so it doesn't match the narration's tense either.

A는 시제는 맞지만 복수, C는 비정형, D는 복수+현재완료로 모두 배제됨. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 동일 결론과 글자 참조를 가지며 오류 없음. 삽입구에 "hands", "waves" 등 복수 명사가 가까이 있어 훑어 읽으면 A로 유인되는 구조이며, 주어 식별+시제 확인의 두 단계 판단이 필요해 medium에 적합하다.

problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: Min-jun saw that his mother had already claimed
his mother, Min-jun saw, had already claimed
the eyes of Min-jun saw that his mother had already claimed

problem.explanation: 분사구 'Setting down the platter...'의 의미상 주어는 바로 뒤 주절의 주어여야 하고, 문맥상 요리를 해서 접시를 내려놓는 사람은 Min-jun이다. A는 Min-jun을 주어로 두고 정동사 saw를 갖춰 주어와 서술어가 모두 맞는다. problem.explanationEn: The opening phrase "Setting down the platter..." describes whoever comes right after the comma, and the context tells you Min-jun cooked and served the meal. Choice A makes Min-jun the subject and gives him a finite verb, "saw," so the modifier and the clause both work. Choice B is a complete sentence, but it says his mother set down the platter, so the modifier is attached to the wrong person. Choice C mentions Min-jun, but the grammatical subject is "the eyes," so his eyes would be setting down the platter. Choice D has the right subject, but "seeing" is a participle, which leaves the sentence without a main verb, so it is a fragment.

problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to show how the visitor's arrival lines up with the timing of Desta's plan. Choice A does this: it states that Desta meant to make her announcement after the first cup and that Almaz knocks before that moment comes. Choice B focuses on Desta's past connection to Almaz but never mentions Desta's plan. Choice C gives the plan and the fact that it doesn't happen, but it leaves out the visitor, so it can't show how her arrival relates to the plan. Choice D only introduces the story and its setting.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — At an Ethiopian coffee ceremony, Desta's unexpected guest—a woman from her village's past—arrives just as Desta was preparing to announce she is leaving forever.

hardJudge.note: 정답 A 검산 일치: 계획 시점(첫 잔 후 발표)과 손님 등장(그 전에 노크)을 함께 연결하는 유일한 선택지. C는 계획·시점·결과를 담지만 손님 누락, B는 손님과 과거 인연만 담고 계획 누락으로 비교가 필요한 강한 오답이며 D도 문맥상 말이 됨. 해설 한/영 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 가상 작가·작품 명시로 저작권 문제 없음. 에티오피아 커피 의식의 세 번째 잔 'baraka' 명칭도 사실에 부합.

advisory.note: B와 C가 각각 요소 하나씩(방문자 / 계획 시점)만 담고 있어서 둘을 비교해야 오답으로 걸러진다. 그래서 medium 난이도에 맞다. D는 너무 쉽게 배제되지만 허용 범위다. 'as soon as'는 노트의 'once'를 바꿔 쓴 표현으로 볼 수 있다.

C does this by linking the net vanishing into the streets to the critics' reading that the net represents the boys' fading friendship. A only describes the setting, the pigeon lofts of Shubra, and never addresses meaning. B accurately retells the plot but never says what the event stands for. D just introduces the author, the date, and the basic event, so it also misses the goal.

hardJudge.note: 정답 C만이 비평가의 상징 해석(그물=사라지는 우정)과 사건을 연결해 '의미'를 설명하므로 옳음. B·D는 노트 정보를 정확히 사용하지만 의미 설명이 없어 비교 후 배제되고, A는 배경만 언급해 가장 약한 오답. 가상의 작품으로 저작권 문제 없음. 표준 SAT rhetorical synthesis 중간 난이도에 부합.

By the third week of the monsoon, the rooftop of the Shanti Niwas building had become a battlefield of clotheslines. When Rajesh stretched a blue tarp above his shirts and declared it "a scientific advantage," Anaya told her sister that she refused to sink to his level; the contest, she insisted, would be won by patience and good wringing alone. ______ by Thursday she had hauled her mother's pedestal fan up four flights of stairs, run an extension cord through the stairwell window, and aimed the whirring blades squarely at her damp dupattas.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

When Rajesh stretched a blue tarp above his shirts and declared it "a scientific advantage," Anaya told her sister that she refused to sink to his level; the contest, she insisted, would be won by patience and good wringing alone. ______ by Thursday she had hauled her mother's pedestal fan up four flights of stairs, run an extension cord through the stairwell window, and aimed the whirring blades squarely at her damp dupattas.

options: Consequently,
Nevertheless,
Similarly,
For example,

A는 Rajesh의 방수포가 그녀의 대응을 불렀다고 볼 수 있어 그럴듯하지만, 바로 앞 문장의 핵심은 '그와 같은 수준으로 내려가지 않겠다'는 다짐이고, 이 다짐에서 선풍기 사용이 결과로 나올 수는 없다. C는 두 사람 모두 장비를 동원했다는 점에서 유사해 보이지만, 이 문장의 초점은 Anaya 자신의 말과 행동이 어긋난다는 데 있다. D는 선풍기 사용을 인내 전략의 한 예로 만들어 버리므로 논리에 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: In the previous sentence, Anaya vows to win with patience and wringing alone instead of copying Rajesh's gadgets. Then the next sentence shows her doing the opposite by dragging a fan up to the roof, so B is correct because it signals a contrast between her vow and what she actually does. A may seem reasonable, since Rajesh's tarp could have provoked her. But the key point of the sentence right before the blank is her promise not to sink to his level, and using a fan can't be a result of that promise. C picks up on the fact that both neighbors end up using equipment, but this sentence is about Anaya's own words clashing with her actions. D doesn't work because it would make the fan an example of her patience-only strategy.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Anaya and her neighbor Rajesh wage an increasingly absurd rooftop monsoon contest to see whose laundry dries fastest during Mumbai's heaviest rains.

hardJudge.note: 앞 문장의 '인내와 짜기만으로' 다짐과 뒤 문장의 선풍기 동원이 명확히 대조되어 B(Nevertheless)가 정답. A는 Rajesh의 방수포→대응이라는 인과로 읽힐 수 있어 유혹적이고, C도 '둘 다 장비 사용'이라는 부분 근거가 있어 비교가 필요함. D는 말이 되나 논리상 배제됨. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 동일 결론과 글자 참조, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 창작 지문으로 저작권 문제 없음. 지문 길이와 두 단계 판단(다짐 파악+행동 대조, 인과 유혹 배제)이 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: 다짐과 실제 행동이 반대로 가는 대조라서 정답 B가 명확하다. A(방수포가 대응을 촉발)와 C(두 사람 모두 장비 사용)는 부분적으로 그럴듯해 오답으로 기능한다. 표준 medium 수준이다.

problem.passage:
On the houseboat drifting through the Kerala backwaters, Deepak turned his grandmother's sandalwood box over in his hands. His aunts had made it clear that they expected him to open it that evening, and he had even pressed his thumb against the brass latch until it gave a small click. ______ he set the box on the shelf beside her old prayer lamp, the latch closed again, deciding that whatever she had kept inside could stay hers a little longer.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: On the houseboat drifting through the Kerala backwaters, Deepak turned his grandmother's sandalwood box over in his hands. His aunts had made it clear that they expected him to open it that evening, and he had even pressed his thumb against the brass latch until it gave a small click. ______ he set the box on the shelf beside her old prayer lamp, the latch closed again, deciding that whatever she had kept inside could stay hers a little longer.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Moreover,
As a result,
Instead,
For instance,
problem.explanation: 앞 문장은 가족의 기대와 걸쇠를 누른 행동으로 상자를 열 것 같은 방향을 제시하고, 빈칸 뒤에서는 상자를 닫은 채 선반에 두기로 한다. 예상된 행동 대신 다른 행동을 택한 것이므로 대안·반전을 나타내는 C가 정답이다. A는 같은 방향의 정보를 덧붙이는 표현인데, 뒤 문장은 앞의 흐름을 뒤집는다. B는 걸쇠를 누른 것이 상자를 닫아 두는 결과로 이어진 것처럼 만들어 인과 방향이 맞지 않는다. D는 뒤 문장을 앞 내용의 예시로 만들지만, 상자를 열지 않는 것은 열려는 기대의 예가 아니다.
problem.explanationEn: The earlier sentence leans toward opening the box: his aunts expect it, and Deepak even clicks the latch. The next sentence goes the other way, because he puts the box away still closed. He chooses a different action from the one that was expected, so the reversal word in C fits. A adds information that continues in the same direction, but this sentence reverses the earlier one. B treats closing the box as a result of pressing the latch, which gets the cause and effect wrong. D presents the sentence as an example, but leaving the box closed is not an example of the expectation that he would open it.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Deepak inherits his grandmother's small sandalwood box on the Kerala houseboat and must decide whether to open it or preserve it unopened.

hardJudge.note: 앞 문장(열 것이라는 기대·걸쇠 클릭)과 뒤 문장(닫은 채 선반에 둠)의 관계는 예상 행동의 대체·반전이므로 'Instead'가 유일하게 성립한다. 뒤 문장의 절대구문("the latch closed again")도 문법적으로 자연스럽다. A(Moreover)는 앞 문장이 행동 나열이라 훑어 읽으면 선택할 수 있고, B(As a result)는 걸쇠를 눌렀다는 직전 행동과 표면적 인과를 만들어 부분적 근거가 있다. D는 명백히 어긋나지만 말은 된다. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 C를 지지하며 글자 참조와 논리가 일치하고, 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 독창적 서사 지문으로 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 기대·걸쇠를 누른 행동 → 닫힌 채 보관으로 이어지는 반전 구조라 Instead가 유일하게 맞다. 걸쇠를 누른 행동이 표면적인 인과 연결을 만들어 B가 그럴듯한 오답이 된다. 중간 난이도의 하단에 해당한다.

problem.passage:
For twenty years, Amaan and Karim had worked side by side at the tannery on the riverbank, dipping hides into the dye pits each morning. Lately, the two partners spoke only about leather______ man could say exactly when the silence between them had begun.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: For twenty years, Amaan and Karim had worked side by side at the tannery on the riverbank, dipping hides into the dye pits each morning. Lately, the two partners spoke only about leather______ man could say exactly when the silence between them had begun.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , neither
neither
; neither
, which neither
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'the two partners spoke only about leather'와 뒤 'neither man could say ...'는 각각 독립절이다. 접속사 없이 두 독립절을 잇는 데는 세미콜론이 맞으므로 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. B는 문장부호 없이 이어 붙인 융합문(run-on)이다. D는 'which'로 관계절을 만들지만 뒤 내용이 관계절 구조에 맞지 않아 비문이 된다.
problem.explanationEn: The text before the blank ("the two partners spoke only about leather") and the text after it ("neither man could say...") are both independent clauses. When you join two independent clauses without a conjunction, a semicolon works, so C is correct. A uses only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B has no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on sentence. D adds "which" to start a relative clause, but the words after it don't fit that structure, so the sentence becomes ungrammatical.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Amaan and Karim, tannery partners at the Moroccan riverside for twenty years, have stopped speaking except to discuss leather, and neither knows when it began.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞뒤 모두 독립절('the two partners spoke only about leather' / 'neither man could say ... begun')이므로 세미콜론(C)이 유일하게 맞음. A는 쉼표 스플라이스, B는 융합문, D는 'which'가 이끄는 관계절이 뒤 구조와 맞지 않아 비문. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답과 선택지 참조가 일치하고 결론이 동일함. 단일 규칙(독립절 연결 부호)으로 풀리고 오답이 전형적 오개념이라 easy에 적합. 사소하게 선택지 B 앞 공백이 두 칸인 점만 표기상 미세한 흠.

advisory.note: 독립절 두 개를 세미콜론으로 잇는 단일 규칙 문항이다. 오답은 쉼표 스플라이스, 융합문, 관계절 오용으로 전형적인 오개념들이다. 선택지 B에 공백이 두 칸 들어간 것은 표시상의 사소한 문제다.

problem.passage:
Kamau sits by the window of the crowded matatu as it lurches down Ngong Road toward the city center. On his wrist is his father's watch, the same one his father carried home from a war many years ago. A jeweler in Nairobi has just finished restoring it. Now the watch, with its newly polished hands, ______ the afternoon light each time the vehicle turns, and the strangers beside him lean closer to study its mended face.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Kamau sits by the window of the crowded matatu as it lurches down Ngong Road toward the city center. On his wrist is his father's watch, the same one his father carried home from a war many years ago. A jeweler in Nairobi has just finished restoring it. Now the watch, with its newly polished hands, ______ the afternoon light each time the vehicle turns, and the strangers beside him lean closer to study its mended face.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: catches
catch
are catching
have caught
problem.explanation: 빈칸에 들어갈 동사의 주어는 단수 명사 'the watch'이고, 'with its newly polished hands'는 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어든 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 단수 현재형 동사가 필요하며, 지문 전체가 현재 시제(sits, lean)로 서술되므로 A가 정답이다. B, C, D는 모두 복수 주어에 맞는 동사형으로, 수식어 속 복수 명사 'hands'를 주어로 착각하게 만드는 오답이다. 문장의 실제 주어는 단수인 'watch'이므로 B, C, D는 수 일치가 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of the verb in the blank is the singular noun "the watch." The phrase "with its newly polished hands" is just a modifier that sits between the subject and the verb. That means you need a singular present-tense verb, and the passage is told in the present tense ("sits," "lean"), so A is correct. B, C, and D are all verb forms that go with plural subjects, and they trick you into treating the plural noun "hands" inside the modifier as the subject. Since the real subject, "watch," is singular, B, C, and D don't agree with it in number.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On a Nairobi matatu, Kamau carries his father's restored watch—the same watch his father carried home from a war—and watches strangers study its repaired face.

hardJudge.note: 주어 'the watch'(단수) + 끼어든 수식어 'with its newly polished hands' 구조. 현재 시제 서술(sits, lean)에 맞춰 단수 현재형 'catches'(A)만 적합. B/C/D는 모두 복수형으로 'hands'에 이끌리는 전형적 오개념 오답. 한·영 해설 모두 정답 및 선택지 참조 일치, 한글 혼입 없음. 단일 규칙(수 일치)으로 해결되어 easy 적합.

advisory.note: 주어 'the watch'(단수)와 동사의 수 일치를 묻는 문항이다. 끼어든 'with its newly polished hands'가 오답을 유도한다. 판단 규칙이 하나뿐이라 easy 수준에 맞다. 오답 B·C·D는 모두 복수형이라 규칙만 알면 바로 걸러진다.

problem.passage:
In the Kyoto pottery district, Akiko and Tomoe once shared a single wheel, laughing as wet clay spun between their hands. Now their two studios face each other across a narrow alley that neither woman ever crosses. Each morning, the row of glazed bowls in Akiko's window ______ in the early light, and each morning Tomoe pretends not to notice them.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In the Kyoto pottery district, Akiko and Tomoe once shared a single wheel, laughing as wet clay spun between their hands. Now their two studios face each other across a narrow alley that neither woman ever crosses. Each morning, the row of glazed bowls in Akiko's window ______ in the early light, and each morning Tomoe pretends not to notice them.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: shine
shines
are shining
have shone
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "row"이고, "of glazed bowls in Akiko's window"는 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 단수 동사가 필요하고, 같은 문장의 "pretends"와 같은 현재 시제여야 하므로 B "shines"가 정답이다. A, C, D는 모두 복수 동사(shine, are, have)를 써서 바로 앞의 복수 명사 "bowls"에 수를 맞춘 오류이다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this clause is the singular noun "row"; the phrase "of glazed bowls in Akiko's window" only modifies it. So you need a singular verb in the present tense, which matches "pretends" later in the sentence. That makes B, "shines," correct. A, C, and D all use plural verb forms (shine, are, have), which wrongly agree with the nearby plural noun "bowls" instead of the actual subject.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In the Kyoto pottery district, Akiko and Tomoe once threw clay together, but now their studios face each other across an alley they never cross.

hardJudge.note: 주어 "row"(단수) + 수식어구 "of glazed bowls in Akiko's window"에 의한 전형적 주어-동사 일치 문항. "each morning ... pretends"가 현재 시제 단서로 작동하여 B "shines"만 적합. A/C/D는 모두 인접 복수 명사 "bowls"에 끌린 복수형 오답으로 오개념 기반 매력도 적절. 해설(한·영) 결론·글자 참조 일치, 한글 혼입 없음. 지문 창작물로 저작권 문제 없음. easy 난이도 적합.

advisory.note: 단수 주어 row와 수식어 of glazed bowls 사이의 주어-동사 수일치 문항으로, 규칙 하나만 알면 풀 수 있다. 오답 A, C, D는 모두 가까운 복수 명사 bowls에 동사를 맞춘 전형적인 오개념이라 easy 난이도에 맞다.

problem.passage:
On the night of his final concert with the Bavarian brass band, Ernst lifted the trumpet his grandfather had repaired decades earlier. He ran his thumb along the bell, feeling each small hollow in the brass. The dents on the old instrument ______ reminders of stories that no one in the band could remember anymore, yet Ernst felt them all as he raised the trumpet to play.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: On the night of his final concert with the Bavarian brass band, Ernst lifted the trumpet his grandfather had repaired decades earlier. He ran his thumb along the bell, feeling each small hollow in the brass. The dents on the old instrument ______ reminders of stories that no one in the band could remember anymore, yet Ernst felt them all as he raised the trumpet to play.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: was
is
were
has been
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 복수 명사 "The dents"이며, "on the old instrument"는 주어를 꾸미는 전치사구일 뿐이다. 또한 이야기가 과거 시제(lifted, ran, felt)로 서술되므로 복수 과거형 동사가 필요하다. 따라서 C "were"가 정답이다. A "was"와 D "has been"은 단수 동사여서 수가 맞지 않으며, 바로 앞의 단수 명사 "instrument"에 이끌려 고르기 쉬운 오답이다. B "is"는 단수인 데다 현재 시제라서 수와 시제가 모두 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is the plural noun "The dents." The phrase "on the old instrument" only describes the subject. The story is also told in the past tense (lifted, ran, felt), so you need a plural past-tense verb. That makes C, "were," the correct answer. A ("was") and D ("has been") are singular verbs, so they don't agree with the subject. They're easy to pick by mistake because the singular noun "instrument" comes right before the blank. B ("is") is wrong on both counts: it's singular, and it's in the present tense.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Ernst, the Bavarian brass band's trumpet player, plays his final concert with an instrument his grandfather repaired, the dents telling stories no one remembers.

hardJudge.note: 주어 "The dents"(복수) + 과거 시제 서술 → "were"가 유일하게 맞음. 오답 3개 모두 단수형으로, 직전 명사 "instrument"에 의한 근접 일치 오개념을 겨냥한 전형적 오답. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답 C와 글자 참조가 일치하고 모순 없음. 단일 규칙·한 단계 추론으로 easy에 적합.

advisory.note: 주어-동사 수 일치 문제로, 주어와 동사 사이에 전치사구가 끼어 있음. 복수 주어 "dents"와 과거 시제 문맥이 맞으므로 정답은 were. 함정이 하나뿐인 전형적인 easy 문항임.

problem.passage:
At the fish camp on Bayou Lafourche, Chet kept his cypress netting needle in his shirt pocket at all times, and for thirty years he had refused to let anyone else use it, not even his own sons. ______ when his cousin Remy, visiting from Texas for only one night, asked to borrow it to mend a torn cast net, Chet handed it over without a word, already suspecting that Remy might leave before dawn and never come back.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: At the fish camp on Bayou Lafourche, Chet kept his cypress netting needle in his shirt pocket at all times, and for thirty years he had refused to let anyone else use it, not even his own sons. ______ when his cousin Remy, visiting from Texas for only one night, asked to borrow it to mend a torn cast net, Chet handed it over without a word, already suspecting that Remy might leave before dawn and never come back.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Similarly,
For example,
Therefore,
Yet
problem.explanation: 첫 문장은 Chet이 30년 동안 아무에게도, 아들에게조차 바늘을 빌려주지 않았다고 말하고, 두 번째 문장은 그가 사촌에게 아무 말 없이 바늘을 건넸다고 한다. 두 문장은 예상과 반대되는 대조 관계이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 비슷한 행동을 덧붙일 때 쓰는데, 바늘을 건넨 행동은 거절하던 습관과 정반대이다. B는 앞 내용의 예시를 들 때 쓰지만, 바늘을 건넨 것은 거절하는 습관의 예가 될 수 없다. C는 결과를 나타내는데, 늘 거절해 왔다는 사실에서 바늘을 건넸다는 결과가 나오지는 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The first sentence tells you that Chet refused for thirty years to let anyone use his needle, not even his sons. The second sentence says he handed it to his cousin without a word. That is the opposite of what you would expect, so the sentences are in contrast, and D is correct. A is for adding a similar action, but handing over the needle goes against his habit of refusing. B introduces an example, but giving the needle away can't be an example of always refusing. C signals a result, and his long refusal doesn't lead to him handing the needle over.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — At a Louisiana bayou fish camp, Chet lends his favorite net-weaving tool to a visiting kinsman and realizes he may never see the man again.

hardJudge.note: 첫 문장(30년간 아무에게도 빌려주지 않음)과 둘째 문장(사촌에게 말없이 건넴)은 명백한 대조 관계로, 유일한 대조 전환어 D "Yet"이 정답임을 직접 검산함. "Yet when ..., Chet handed it over"는 문법적으로도 자연스러움. 오답 A(유사), B(예시), C(결과)는 전형적 오개념 선택지로 적절. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 D를 일관되게 뒷받침하며 글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 단일 규칙·한 단계 추론으로 easy 난이도에 부합. 원작 지문은 창작으로 보이며 저작권 의심 없음.

advisory.note: 명확한 대조 관계. 'Yet' 뒤 쉼표 없음은 SAT 관례상 허용. 오답들은 전형적인 오개념이다.

problem.passage:
Sophia stood at the ferry kiosk on the island of Naxos, holding a ticket she had not yet decided to use. Thirty years earlier, she had promised an old sailor named Stavros that she would come back every summer to wait for his boat at this very dock. She had kept that promise for exactly one summer. ______ she had moved to Athens, married, and let the island fade into a story she rarely told.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: Sophia stood at the ferry kiosk on the island of Naxos, holding a ticket she had not yet decided to use. Thirty years earlier, she had promised an old sailor named Stavros that she would come back every summer to wait for his boat at this very dock. She had kept that promise for exactly one summer. ______ she had moved to Athens, married, and let the island fade into a story she rarely told.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: After that,
For example,
In contrast,
Similarly,
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 문장은 소피아가 약속을 단 한 번의 여름 동안만 지켰다고 말하고, 뒤 문장은 그 이후 그녀가 아테네로 이사하고 결혼한 일을 말하므로 시간 순서를 잇는 A가 정답이다. B는 예시를 나타내지만, 이사와 결혼은 한 번 약속을 지킨 일의 예가 아니다. C는 대조를 나타내는데, 뒤 문장은 앞 문장과 맞서는 내용이 아니라 그다음에 일어난 일이다. D는 비슷한 내용을 나타내지만 두 문장은 비슷한 행동을 말하고 있지 않다.
problem.explanationEn: The sentence before the blank says Sophia kept her promise for only one summer. The sentence after it tells what happened next: she moved to Athens and got married. Since these events come one after another in time, A is correct. B signals an example, but moving and marrying aren't examples of keeping the promise once. C signals a contrast, but the second sentence doesn't oppose the first; it simply continues the story in time. D signals similarity, but the two sentences don't describe similar actions.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On a Greek island ferry kiosk, Sophia remembers she once promised an old sailor she would return to wait for his boat, a vow she abandoned thirty years ago.

hardJudge.note: 앞 문장(한 번의 여름 동안 약속 이행) → 뒤 문장(아테네 이주·결혼·섬을 잊음)은 명백한 시간적 순서이므로 'After that,'(A)이 유일하게 논리적임. B(예시)·D(유사)는 관계 불일치, C(대조)는 뒤 문장이 앞 문장과 맞서는 내용이 아니므로 배제됨. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 A를 일관되게 지지하고 선택지 글자 참조가 정확하며 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 서술은 창작 지문으로 저작권 우려 없음. 시간 순서 전환어라는 단일 개념으로 한 단계 추론만 필요해 easy에 적합.

advisory.note: The answer depends on one clue that sits right next to the blank: "for exactly one summer" leads into what happened next, so the time-sequence transition is correct. C is a believable wrong answer because keeping the promise and then dropping it can look like a contrast, but the sequence reading fits better. Overall the item suits the easy level.

problem.stimulus:

problem.question: The student wants to describe the surprising event at the center of the story. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In Lena Haubrich's 2019 short story "The Dented Bell," a brass band in a small Bavarian village holds its weekly rehearsal.
In Lena Haubrich's short story "The Dented Bell," Anton's tuba, damaged in a fall from his bicycle, produces a softer and warmer tone than the band has ever heard.
In Lena Haubrich's short story "The Dented Bell," which was translated into English in 2022, the main character is an elderly tuba player named Anton.
In Lena Haubrich's short story "The Dented Bell," Anton's tuba is repaired after a fall from his bicycle so that it sounds the same as it always did.
problem.explanation: 목표는 이야기 중심의 놀라운 사건을 묘사하는 것이다. B는 망가진 튜바가 오히려 밴드가 들어 본 적 없는 부드럽고 따뜻한 소리를 낸다는 점을 전해 목표에 맞는다. A는 배경(마을, 연습)만 소개하고 놀라운 사건이 없다. C는 번역 연도와 주인공 소개일 뿐 사건을 다루지 않는다. D는 튜바가 수리되어 예전과 같은 소리를 낸다고 해 메모 내용과 어긋나는 부정확한 진술이다.
problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to describe the surprising event at the heart of the story. B does this: it explains that Anton's tuba, damaged in a fall, makes a softer and warmer tone than the band has ever heard. A only gives the setting (the village and the rehearsal) and doesn't mention anything surprising. C tells you the translation date and introduces the main character, but it doesn't describe an event. D is inaccurate, because the notes never say the tuba is repaired or that it sounds the same as before.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — At a Bavarian village brass band rehearsal, the tuba player arrives with a malfunctioning instrument that somehow sounds more beautiful broken than it ever did whole.

hardJudge.note: B가 "놀라운 사건"(망가진 튜바가 더 좋은 소리를 냄)을 메모 그대로 정확히 전달한다. A·C는 목표(사건 묘사)와 무관한 배경·메타 정보, D는 메모에 없는 내용(수리, 동일한 소리)으로 부정확하여 배제된다. 한·영 해설 모두 B를 일관되게 뒷받침하며 선택지 참조가 일치하고 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 단일 규칙(목표에 맞는 관련 정보 선택)으로 풀리고 단서가 명시적이어서 easy 적합. 가상의 작가·작품으로 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 목표와 일치하는 단서가 명확하고, 오답은 배경만 소개하거나 사건을 다루지 않거나 메모 내용과 어긋나는 전형적 유형이다. D는 메모에 없는 내용이라 쉽게 배제되지만 easy 수준에서는 허용된다.

B only describes what the old man does, so it has neither the main character nor the setting. D mentions a boy's question but doesn't give his name or say where the story happens.

hardJudge.note: 정답 C만 주인공(Tuan)과 배경(하노이 골목, 새벽)을 모두 포함. A·B는 노인 중심, D는 소년을 언급하나 이름·배경 없음 — 전형적 오답. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 일치하고 정확함. 가상의 작품으로 저작권 문제 없음. 두 요소 매칭만으로 풀리는 easy 적합.

problem.passage:
Around 1415, the Florentine architect Filippo Brunelleschi painted a small panel of the Baptistery of San Giovanni as seen from the doorway of the cathedral opposite it. He drilled a hole through the panel so that a viewer could stand where he had stood, look through the back, and check the painted image against the real building reflected in a handheld mirror. Brunelleschi's skill had come from years of measuring ruined Roman buildings and drawing plans for builders, work that required him to turn three-dimensional spaces into exact lines on a flat surface.

Brunelleschi never wrote down his method, however. What we know of the demonstration comes mostly from a biography written decades later by Antonio Manetti. It was the humanist Leon Battista Alberti who, in his 1435 treatise On Painting, explained linear perspective as a set of geometric steps that any painter could follow. Historians therefore credit Brunelleschi with showing that a single fixed viewpoint could produce a convincing image, and they credit Alberti with turning that demonstration into a method that could be taught.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

B는 측량 훈련이라는 세부 내용을 다루지만, 지문은 그 훈련이 화가로서의 일보다 더 중요했다고 비교하지 않는다. C는 알베르티의 역할을 언급하지만 브루넬레스키가 방법을 기록했다고 하여 지문의 'never wrote down'과 모순된다. D는 마네티의 전기라는 세부 사항을 가져오지만, 역사가들이 시연 자체를 의심한다는 내용은 지문 어디에도 없다.
problem.explanationEn: A is correct. The first paragraph describes Brunelleschi's demonstration, which grew out of his experience measuring buildings. The second paragraph explains that he never recorded his method and that Alberti turned it into steps painters could learn, so A is the only choice that covers both paragraphs. B picks up the detail about his surveying training, but the text never says that training mattered more than his painting. C mentions Alberti's role, but it claims Brunelleschi wrote down the method, which contradicts the text's statement that he "never wrote down his method." D draws on the detail about Manetti's biography, but nothing in the text says historians doubt the experiment happened.

problem.passage:
In his 1880 essay "The Experimental Novel," Émile Zola argued that the novelist should work like a physiologist, placing characters in carefully observed conditions and recording how heredity and environment shape their behavior. Critics often mocked this analogy, pointing out that a novelist, unlike a scientist, invents both the experiment and its outcome. Yet Zola's working notebooks suggest that the analogy guided his practice more than his critics assumed. Before drafting Germinal (1885), he spent a week in the mining region near Anzin, descending into a pit, interviewing workers, and sketching the layout of miners' cottages; for other novels he compiled files of newspaper clippings, railway timetables, and department-store catalogs. Literary historians who have examined these files note that Zola rarely altered the documented details to suit his plots. Instead, he frequently revised plot events that conflicted with what he had recorded, letting the gathered evidence constrain what his imagined characters could plausibly do.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

problem.passage:
Before 1908, even the most chromatic Western music still relied on an underlying hierarchy: dissonant chords, however lush, were heard as tensions that would eventually resolve to a stable tonic. In works such as his Second String Quartet and the piano pieces of Op. 11, Arnold Schoenberg abandoned that expectation. Critics at the time often described the results as chaotic, assuming that without a home key the music lacked any organizing logic. Yet Schoenberg's scores reveal a different kind of coherence. Rather than treating dissonances as unstable sounds requiring resolution, he let them stand as independent sonorities, and he unified passages by repeating and transforming small groups of intervals, so that a brief melodic cell might reappear as a chord, in inversion, or at a new pitch level. What listeners perceived as disorder was, in this view, a shift from organization by key to organization by intervallic motive.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

A is right that critics called the music chaotic, but the text never says later audiences came to prefer it. B gets the heightened dissonance right, but the text says the dissonances were not resolved, which is the opposite of what B claims. D accurately reports that the music had no home key and that critics saw no logic in it, but it misses the text's main point, which is to argue against that critical view.

problem.passage:
Modern readers often assume that Sappho's poems survive only in tatters because ancient readers found her expressions of desire for women too troubling to preserve. The evidence of transmission, however, points elsewhere. Classicist Camille Hardwick notes that Sappho wrote in the Aeolic dialect of Lesbos, whose unfamiliar vowels and word forms made her verses increasingly difficult for later Greek scribes and schoolteachers to read. As literary education across the Greek-speaking world came to favor Attic and Ionic authors, copies of Sappho were made less often, and her collected books gradually fell out of circulation.

Hardwick points out that this explanation also fits what does survive. Many of the fragments, including lines frankly describing longing for a woman, were preserved because grammarians and critics quoted them to illustrate rare Aeolic words or admirable meter, and others turned up on discarded papyri in Egyptian rubbish heaps. If ancient copyists had been purging erotic content, Hardwick argues, such passages would hardly be among the pieces that reached us.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

problem.passage:
In the 1940s, the architect Le Corbusier introduced the Modulor, a system of measurements derived from the height of a standing man with a raised arm and subdivided according to the golden ratio. Le Corbusier promoted it as a rational tool that would bring universal harmony to building design, and he applied it to projects such as the Unité d'Habitation in Marseille, where ceiling heights, window bands, and balcony depths all follow its intervals. Yet architectural historians who have examined his working drawings note that Le Corbusier frequently departed from the Modulor's figures when they conflicted with site conditions, construction budgets, or simply his own visual judgment. In their view, the system functioned less as a strict generator of form than as a flexible vocabulary that lent his intuitive choices the appearance of mathematical necessity.

Based on the text, what have architectural historians concluded about Le Corbusier's use of the Modulor?

Literary historians have often described the inward turn of early twentieth-century Japanese fiction as an import, a technique borrowed from European modernists. Natsume Soseki's novel Kusamakura (1906), however, complicates that account.
