In 1964, philosopher Arthur Danto encountered Andy Warhol's Brillo Box, a plywood sculpture that looked almost exactly like the cardboard cartons of soap pads stacked in any supermarket stockroom. The experience convinced Danto that no visible property could explain why one object was art and its twin was not. __Earlier theorists had assumed that art could be identified by looking, whether by its beauty, its skill of execution, or its resemblance to the world.__ Danto argued instead that what makes something an artwork is its place within an "artworld": a surrounding atmosphere of theory and a knowledge of art history that lets an object be interpreted as being about something. On this view, Warhol's box counts as art not because of how it looks but because it embodies a meaning that viewers familiar with that context can read in it.

The poem's second section, which opens with the famous image of "Time's wingèd chariot hurrying ______ that leisure is impossible: the grave, the speaker warns, offers no embraces. Only in the final section does he urge immediate pleasure as the logical conclusion.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

A는 and 때문에 insists가 관계절 안의 두 번째 동사(opens and insists)가 되어 주절에 본동사가 남지 않는다. B는 세미콜론 앞부분이 동사 없는 불완전한 절이 되고, 닫는 쉼표도 빠져 있다. D는 대명사 it이 주어를 한 번 더 써서 원래 주어가 동사를 잃고, 대시로 연 삽입도 쉼표와 짝이 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject "The poem's second section" is interrupted by a nonessential relative clause that begins with a comma ("which opens ... near"). That clause has to close with a comma, and then the main verb, "insists," comes right after it. That's why C is correct. A adds "and," which makes "insists" a second verb inside the relative clause ("opens and insists"), so the sentence ends up with no main verb. B puts a semicolon after a subject that has no verb, so the part before the semicolon isn't a complete clause, and the closing comma is missing too. D adds the pronoun "it," which repeats the subject and leaves the original subject without a verb; it also mixes a dash with the opening comma, so the interruption isn't punctuated consistently.

problem.passage:
In the 1960s and 1970s, developmental psychologist Mary Ainsworth designed the Strange Situation, a laboratory procedure in which a one-year-old is briefly separated from its mother, left with a stranger, and then reunited with the mother. Many observers assumed the most revealing moment would be the separation itself, since an infant who cries loudly when the mother leaves seems to be the most strongly attached. Ainsworth, however, paid closest attention to the reunion. Some infants who had cried hard calmed quickly once the mother came back and went back to exploring the room, and Ainsworth classified them as securely attached. Others who had cried just as hard pushed the mother away or would not be comforted, and some infants who had shown no distress at all avoided the mother when she returned. Ainsworth had also watched these families at home earlier, and she found that the infants classified as secure usually had mothers who responded promptly and sensitively to their signals there.

According to the text, what did Ainsworth treat as the clearest evidence of how an infant was attached to its mother?

A describes what other observers assumed, and the text sets Ainsworth's view against that assumption. B mentions the stranger, who is part of the procedure, but the text never says the infant's reaction to the stranger was used to classify attachment. C goes too far: the text says home responsiveness was linked to the secure classification, not that it alone decided the classification.

problem.passage:
In the 1960s and 1970s, British sociologist Basil Bernstein proposed that children from different social classes tend to develop distinct ways of using language. He described a "restricted code," which relies on meanings shared within a close-knit group and leaves much unstated, and an "elaborated code," which spells out meanings explicitly so that listeners unfamiliar with the speaker's context can follow. Bernstein observed that working-class children often favored the restricted code, while middle-class children were more practiced in both. Critics sometimes read his work as claiming that working-class speech was deficient, but Bernstein rejected that interpretation. His central argument concerned schools: because British classrooms rewarded the explicit, context-independent style of the elaborated code, children who arrived already fluent in it were advantaged, and the resulting gaps in achievement reflected the expectations built into schooling rather than differences in children's linguistic or intellectual ability.

According to the text, what did Bernstein see as the main source of the achievement differences he discussed?

A gets the restricted code's reliance on unstated meaning right, but calling that a weakness is the "deficient" reading that Bernstein rejected. In the 1970s, anthropologist Barbara Myerhoff spent several years at a senior center in Venice, California, whose members were mostly elderly Jewish immigrants from Eastern Europe. Many observers had described such communities as remnants, groups simply waiting out the end of a vanishing way of life. For centuries, philosophers treated categories the way Aristotle did: a thing belongs to a category if it meets a fixed list of necessary and sufficient conditions, and every member belongs equally. In the early 1970s, psychologist Eleanor Rosch tested this assumption with the Dani people of New Guinea, whose language has only two basic color terms, roughly "dark" and "light." Rosch found that Dani participants learned and remembered new names more easily when the names were attached to certain "focal" colors, such as a particular vivid red, than when they were attached to colors falling between those focal points. __Because the Dani had no word for red, they could not have picked up this preference from their vocabulary, so the advantage seemed to come from how human perception organizes color itself.__ Rosch went on to argue that categories are built around such best examples, or prototypes, with other members belonging more or less strongly depending on how closely they resemble the center.

problem.passage:
When European diplomats gathered in Berlin in 1884 to settle competing claims in Africa, no African ruler or representative was invited. Popular accounts often say the conference carved up the continent on a map, but historians point out that the delegates actually drew few borders there. Instead, they agreed on procedures: a power claiming coastal territory had to notify the other signatories, and a claim would be recognized only if the power showed "effective occupation," meaning enough administrative presence to protect trade and maintain order. Those rules turned out to matter more than any line drawn in the meeting hall. Because recognition now depended on showing control on the ground, European states rushed to sign treaties with local leaders, set up outposts, and send military expeditions into the interior, so the partition sped up sharply in the years after the conference. In this way, the agreement in Berlin, made without any African participants, set off a scramble whose effects African societies would feel for generations.

problem.passage:
Many accounts of the 1956 Suez Crisis treat it as the moment Britain's imperial decline became visible to the world. When Egyptian President Gamal Abdel Nasser nationalized the Suez Canal Company in July of that year, Britain, together with France and Israel, launched a military intervention to regain control of the waterway. Within weeks, financial pressure from the United States forced a humiliating British withdrawal. __Yet historian Wm. Roger Louis has argued that the crisis did less to cause Britain's retreat from empire than to expose a weakness that officials in London had privately acknowledged for years.__ In his reading, the canal episode mattered chiefly because it stripped away the public pretense that Britain could still act as a great power independent of Washington.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: Many accounts of the 1956 Suez Crisis treat it as the moment Britain's imperial decline became visible to the world. When Egyptian President Gamal Abdel Nasser nationalized the Suez Canal Company in July of that year, Britain, together with France and Israel, launched a military intervention to regain control of the waterway. Within weeks, financial pressure from the United States forced a humiliating British withdrawal. __Yet historian Wm. Roger Louis has argued that the crisis did less to cause Britain's retreat from empire than to expose a weakness that officials in London had privately acknowledged for years.__ In his reading, the canal episode mattered chiefly because it stripped away the public pretense that Britain could still act as a great power independent of Washington.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents evidence that the British withdrawal from Egypt was caused mainly by American financial pressure.
It explains why Nasser chose to nationalize the canal company at that particular moment in 1956.
It introduces a scholar's view that qualifies the common account of the crisis's significance described earlier.
It concludes that the Suez Crisis had little effect on how Britain was perceived internationally.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 시작해 앞의 통설(수에즈 위기가 영국 쇠퇴가 드러난 순간)을 소개한 뒤, Louis가 위기는 쇠퇴의 원인이라기보다 이미 알려진 약점을 드러냈다고 본다는 수정적 견해를 제시하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 미국의 재정 압박이 앞 문장에 나오지만 밑줄 문장은 철수 원인의 증거를 제시하지 않는다. B는 나세르의 국유화 동기를 다루지 않으므로 틀리다. D는 마지막 문장이 위기가 영국의 '공적 가식'을 벗겨냈다고 하므로 국제적 인식에 큰 영향이 있었다는 내용과 모순된다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence begins with "Yet," which signals a turn away from the common account given earlier (that Suez was the moment Britain's decline became visible). It then presents Louis's more nuanced view: the crisis exposed a weakness instead of causing it. That makes C correct. A is wrong because American financial pressure is mentioned in the previous sentence, and the underlined sentence offers no evidence about why Britain withdrew. B is wrong because the sentence never discusses Nasser's motives. D is wrong because the final sentence says the crisis stripped away Britain's public pretense, so it clearly did change how Britain was seen.

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 통설과 대비되는 Louis의 수정적 견해를 도입하므로 C가 정확함. A(미국 재정 압박 언급)와 D(인식 변화 관련)는 지문 내용에 부분적 근거가 있어 비교가 필요하고, B는 가장 약하나 지문 소재상 말이 됨. 한·영 해설 모두 동일 결론·글자 참조, 모순 없음. Wm. Roger Louis의 입장 서술도 실제 학계 견해와 어긋나지 않음. 다만 통설 자체가 '쇠퇴가 가시화된 순간'이라 Louis 견해와의 대비가 다소 미묘한 편이나 '원인 vs. 노출' 구도로 충분히 성립함.

advisory.note: 지문 논리에 미세한 약점이 있다. 통설은 위기를 '쇠퇴가 가시화된 순간'으로 기술할 뿐 '원인'으로 보지는 않는데, Louis는 '원인이라기보다'라고 반박한다. 'qualifies'라는 표현이 이 약점을 덮어 주므로 정답 C는 유효하다. A와 D는 부분적인 근거가 있지만 B는 쉽게 배제되어, medium 난이도의 하단에 해당한다.

problem.passage:
Historians have long described Britain's Great Reform Act of 1832 as the moment the middle class entered political life. The act did extend the vote to many householders in towns, raising the electorate from roughly 400,000 to about 650,000 men. __Yet historian Philip Salmon argues that the act's most lasting effect came not from who could vote but from a new requirement that voters register in advance.__ Because registration could be challenged in annual courts, local party associations formed to sign up supporters and dispute opponents' claims, and these associations became permanent organizations that drew middle-class men into politics between elections.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It introduces a view that moves attention from the act's expansion of the electorate to a procedural feature that the rest of the text then explains.
It introduces a view that rejects the claim that the act increased the number of voters, which the rest of the text then disproves.

problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 시작해 선거권 확대라는 기존 초점에서 사전 등록 요건이라는 절차적 특징으로 관심을 옮기고, 이어지는 문장이 등록 법정과 정당 조직 형성으로 그 영향을 설명하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 문장이 대조를 이룬다는 점은 맞지만, Salmon은 유권자 수 증가를 부정하지 않고 다른 효과가 더 지속적이었다고 말할 뿐이다. C는 앞 문장의 수치와 연결되는 듯하지만 밑줄 문장은 수치를 요약하지 않으며 뒤에도 추가 수치가 없다. D는 '전환점'이라는 앞 내용과 이어지지만, 밑줄 문장은 기존 평가의 이유를 설명하는 것이 아니라 다른 해석을 내놓는다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence begins with "Yet" and moves attention from the act's widening of the vote to a procedural feature, advance registration. The next sentence then explains how registration courts led to permanent party associations, so A is correct. B gets the contrast right, but Salmon never denies that the electorate grew; he only argues that another effect lasted longer. C ties the sentence to the earlier figures, but the sentence doesn't summarize those numbers, and no new figures come after it. D links to the "turning point" idea, but the sentence offers a different interpretation rather than explaining the traditional one.

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 선거권 확대(앞 문장)에서 사전 등록 요건(절차적 특징)으로 초점을 옮기고, 마지막 문장이 그 요건의 결과(등록 법정→정당 조직)를 설명하므로 A가 정확함. B는 Salmon이 유권자 증가를 부정하지 않으므로 오답, C는 수치 요약·추가 수치 없음, D는 기존 평가의 이유 설명이 아니라 대안 해석 제시이므로 오답. 1832년 개혁법 유권자 수(약 40만→65만)와 Philip Salmon의 등록제 중심 해석은 실제 학설과 부합. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 동일 결론과 선택지 참조로 일관되며 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 오답 세 개 모두 지문의 일부 요소(대조, 수치, '전환점')와 연결되는 부분적 근거를 가져 medium 난이도에 적합.

advisory.note: 유권자 수 약 40만→65만은 통설 수치(약 43.5만→65.2만)와 대체로 맞는다. 등록 요건과 정당 조직 형성에 관한 Salmon의 논지도 실제 연구(Electoral Reform at Work)와 일치한다. B와 D는 일부만 맞는 근거를 갖고 있어 비교해야 배제된다. C는 다소 약한 오답이지만 말은 된다.

problem.passage:
Lloyd's of London is often described as an insurance company, but it is better understood as a marketplace. Rather than a single firm setting prices, dozens of independent syndicates—groups of investors backing a specialist underwriter—compete to take on portions of a given risk. When a shipowner seeks coverage for a vessel crossing a hazardous strait, a broker carries the proposal from one syndicate to another. A "lead" underwriter, typically one with recognized expertise in that type of voyage, examines the ship's age, cargo, route, and crew record and proposes a premium; other syndicates may then accept a share of the risk on those terms or decline.

Economic historians argue that this arrangement allowed maritime risk to be priced more accurately than a single insurer could manage. Because each underwriter staked capital on its own judgment, poorly reasoned quotes were quickly exposed when other syndicates refused to follow them, while a lead underwriter whose assessments proved reliable attracted more followers over time. The market's prices, in this view, reflected the pooled scrutiny of many specialists rather than the estimate of any one of them.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

D takes details from the example (the strait, the crew record) and turns them into a general rule the text never states.

advisory.note: B는 구조 설명과 경제사가들의 평가(is credited with)를 함께 담고 있다. A와 C는 지문에 나온 세부 사항(리드 언더라이터, 브로커)에 근거하지만 메커니즘을 왜곡한다. D는 예시를 지나치게 일반화했다. 중간 난이도에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
In the Democratic Republic of the Congo, a large share of cobalt is dug by hand rather than by industrial firms, and in 2019 the government created a state company, Entreprise Générale du Cobalt (EGC), with exclusive rights to buy and export this artisanal output. Officials argued that a single buyer would let them trace the metal, enforce safety rules, and capture revenue that had been lost to middlemen. Economist Raphaël Kabeya, however, found that most hand-dug cobalt never reached EGC. Diggers kept selling to independent trading depots, which paid cash on the spot and accepted ore in any quantity, while EGC paid only after the ore had been tested and graded. Kabeya argues that the monopoly failed not because miners rejected regulation itself but because the official channel could not match the speed and flexibility that cash-poor diggers depended on.

Based on the text, what does Kabeya conclude about why artisanal miners went around EGC?

problem.passage:
In the seventeenth century, the Dutch Republic controlled much of northern Europe's trade in preserved herring, a position historians often credit simply to the Dutch fleet's size. Economic historian Jan de Vries and others point to a more specific combination of innovations. Dutch crews gutted and salted herring aboard large decked vessels called busses, so the fish could be packed in barrels at sea rather than spoiling on the way to port. The fluyt, a cargo ship developed in the 1590s, then moved those barrels cheaply across the Baltic and beyond: its rounded hull held unusually large cargoes, and its simple rigging let it sail with roughly half the crew that rival ships of similar size needed. Because preservation at sea kept the product's quality steady and the fluyt cut the cost of shipping each barrel, Dutch merchants could sell reliable herring at prices competitors struggled to match.

According to the text, what accounted for the Dutch advantage in the preserved herring trade?

The fluyt, a cargo ship developed in the 1590s, then moved those barrels cheaply across the Baltic and beyond: its rounded hull held unusually large cargoes, and its simple rigging let it sail with roughly half the crew that rival ships of similar size needed. Because preservation at sea kept the product's quality steady and the fluyt cut the cost of shipping each barrel, Dutch merchants could sell reliable herring at prices competitors struggled to match.
problem.question: According to the text, what accounted for the Dutch advantage in the preserved herring trade?
options: The Dutch fleet's sheer size allowed it to catch more herring than any rival nation could catch.
The fluyt's large rounded hull allowed Dutch crews to gut and salt herring while still at sea.
The busses' small crews made it inexpensive for Dutch merchants to carry herring across the Baltic.
The pairing of at-sea processing with a low-cost cargo ship allowed Dutch merchants to offer dependable fish cheaply.
problem.explanation: 지문은 두 가지 혁신을 함께 제시한다. 버스선에서 바다 위에 가공해 품질을 유지한 것과, 플루이트선으로 운송비를 낮춘 것이 결합해 우위를 만들었다고 하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 지문이 흔한 설명으로 소개한 뒤 더 구체적인 설명으로 대체하는 견해다. B는 바다 위 가공을 플루이트선의 일로 잘못 연결했는데, 실제로 가공은 버스선에서 이루어졌다. C는 적은 선원 수라는 특징을 플루이트선이 아닌 버스선에 잘못 붙였다.
problem.explanationEn: The text names two innovations that worked together: processing fish at sea on busses kept quality steady, and the fluyt lowered the shipping cost per barrel. Because the Dutch combined these two, D is correct. A states the common explanation, which the text brings up only to replace it with a more specific one. B attaches at-sea gutting and salting to the fluyt, but that work happened on the busses. C gives the busses the small-crew feature, but the text says that belonged to the fluyt.

quality.seed: economics and business — Dutch Golden Age herring fishery and the fluyt ship design enabling preserved fish export market dominance

hardJudge.note: 정답 D는 지문 마지막 문장("Because preservation at sea kept the product's quality steady and the fluyt cut the cost... reliable herring at prices competitors struggled to match")을 정확히 종합한다. A는 지문이 반박하는 통념, B·C는 버스선/플루이트선의 특징을 서로 바꿔 붙인 세부 혼동형 오답으로, 두 선박의 역할을 각각 확인해야 배제되므로 medium 2단계 판단 요건에 부합한다. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 D를 지지하고 글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 역사적 사실(버스선 선상 가공, 1590년대 플루이트, 적은 선원 수, de Vries)도 통설과 부합하며 서술 자체는 독창적 산문으로 저작권 우려 없음.

advisory.note: B와 C는 지문 속 두 배의 특징을 서로 바꿔 붙인 오답이라 정독해야만 걸러낼 수 있다. A는 지문이 흔한 통념으로 소개한 견해라 그럴듯하게 읽힌다. 정답 D는 지문의 마지막 문장을 바꿔 말한 것이다. medium 난이도에 맞는다.

problem.passage:
Economists studying Bangladesh's garment industry have long described it as a textbook case of a buyer-driven supply chain: large Western retailers set prices and delivery deadlines, and factories compete fiercely to win orders by keeping labor costs low. Researcher Nazia Rahman argues that this picture, while accurate at the top of the chain, obscures what happens below it. In her surveys of Dhaka's industrial suburbs, many registered factories that accepted orders from international buyers did not complete the work themselves. __Instead, they quietly passed portions of each order to smaller, unregistered workshops, which were paid per piece and absorbed sudden spikes in volume when deadlines tightened.__ Because these workshops fall outside inspection regimes, Rahman contends, the cost pressure that retailers apply is not simply borne by the visible factories; it is pushed downward to the least protected workers in the network.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: Economists studying Bangladesh's garment industry have long described it as a textbook case of a buyer-driven supply chain: large Western retailers set prices and delivery deadlines, and factories compete fiercely to win orders by keeping labor costs low. Researcher Nazia Rahman argues that this picture, while accurate at the top of the chain, obscures what happens below it. In her surveys of Dhaka's industrial suburbs, many registered factories that accepted orders from international buyers did not complete the work themselves. __Instead, they quietly passed portions of each order to smaller, unregistered workshops, which were paid per piece and absorbed sudden spikes in volume when deadlines tightened.__ Because these workshops fall outside inspection regimes, Rahman contends, the cost pressure that retailers apply is not simply borne by the visible factories; it is pushed downward to the least protected workers in the network.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It specifies a practice that supports the researcher's claim that the conventional account leaves out part of the chain's operation.
It specifies a practice that explains why retailers are able to set prices and deadlines for registered factories.
It specifies a practice that the researcher offers as a solution to the problem of weak inspection regimes.
It specifies a practice that challenges the researcher's conclusion about where cost pressure ultimately falls.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 등록 공장이 주문 일부를 비등록 작업장에 넘긴다는 구체적 관행을 제시하며, 이는 기존 설명이 공급망 하층을 가린다는 Rahman의 주장을 뒷받침하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 소매업체의 가격 결정력이 지문 첫 문장에 나오지만 밑줄 문장은 그 원인을 설명하지 않는다. C는 검사 제도가 언급되긴 하나 하도급은 해결책이 아니라 문제의 일부로 제시된다. D는 밑줄 문장이 비용 압력이 하층 노동자에게 전가된다는 결론을 반박하는 것이 아니라 오히려 그 근거가 되므로 틀리다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence describes a concrete practice: registered factories handing parts of orders to unregistered workshops. This backs up Rahman's claim that the standard buyer-driven account hides what happens lower in the chain, so A is correct. B is wrong because the text mentions retailers' power to set prices, but the underlined sentence doesn't explain where that power comes from. C is wrong because inspection regimes do come up, but subcontracting is presented as part of the problem, not as a solution. D is wrong because the sentence supports Rahman's conclusion that cost pressure is pushed down to the least protected workers. It doesn't challenge it.

quality.seed: economics and business — Bangladeshi garment factory subcontracting networks and buyer-driven global supply chain labor cost competition

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 "Instead"로 앞 문장(등록 공장이 직접 작업하지 않음)을 받아 하도급 관행을 구체화하며, 이는 "기존 설명이 하층을 가린다"는 Rahman의 주장을 뒷받침함 → A 정답 확인. B(소매업체 가격 결정력의 원인), C(해결책), D(결론 반박)는 모두 지문과 불일치. B·C는 지문 속 요소(소매업체, 검사 제도)를 차용해 부분적 타당성을 가지며, D는 방향 반전 오답으로 비교적 쉽게 배제되지만 말은 됨. 두 단계 판단(문장 내용 파악 + Rahman 주장과의 연결) 요구로 medium 적합. 해설 한·영 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음, 자연스러움. 가상의 연구자 인용으로 사실 오류·저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 정답 A가 맞다. 선택지 모두 'It specifies a practice that…'로 시작하는 평행 구조라서 기능을 구분해 읽어야 한다. B와 C는 지문 속 요소(가격 결정력, 검사 제도)를 끌어와 그럴듯하게 만들었고, D는 방향을 뒤집은 오답이다. medium 난이도에 맞다.

problem.passage:
In nineteenth-century Australia, colonial governments leased vast inland tracts to pastoralists rather than selling them outright, and many historians have treated these pastoral leases chiefly as a tool for controlling who could occupy land. Economic historian Lena Marchetti argues that the leases also shaped how meat reached growing coastal cities. Because leaseholders lacked secure long-term title, they had little incentive to build costly fencing or local slaughter facilities; instead, they relied on drovers who walked mobs of cattle hundreds of kilometers along stock routes to urban saleyards. __Marchetti notes that stock routes thickened noticeably in districts where leases were shortest, while regions granted longer tenures developed more on-station infrastructure and fewer droving corridors.__ In her view, then, the droving networks that fed Sydney and Melbourne were not simply a response to distance but partly a product of land policy.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: In nineteenth-century Australia, colonial governments leased vast inland tracts to pastoralists rather than selling them outright, and many historians have treated these pastoral leases chiefly as a tool for controlling who could occupy land. Economic historian Lena Marchetti argues that the leases also shaped how meat reached growing coastal cities. Because leaseholders lacked secure long-term title, they had little incentive to build costly fencing or local slaughter facilities; instead, they relied on drovers who walked mobs of cattle hundreds of kilometers along stock routes to urban saleyards. __Marchetti notes that stock routes thickened noticeably in districts where leases were shortest, while regions granted longer tenures developed more on-station infrastructure and fewer droving corridors.__ In her view, then, the droving networks that fed Sydney and Melbourne were not simply a response to distance but partly a product of land policy.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a view held by many historians that Marchetti ultimately rejects as unsupported by the evidence.
It offers a pattern that supports Marchetti's claim that lease conditions influenced how cattle were moved to cities.
It explains why drovers preferred to walk cattle along stock routes rather than use on-station slaughter facilities.
It offers a pattern that suggests distance alone, rather than lease conditions, determined where droving corridors formed.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 임차 기간이 짧은 지역일수록 가축 이동로가 많고 긴 지역일수록 현지 시설이 많았다는 패턴을 제시해, 임대 정책이 육류 공급 방식을 형성했다는 Marchetti의 주장을 뒷받침하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 역사가들의 일반적 견해가 첫 문장에 나오지만 밑줄 문장은 그 견해가 아니라 Marchetti의 근거이므로 틀렸다. C는 투자 유인 부족을 설명한 것은 앞 문장이며, 밑줄 문장은 드로버의 선호를 설명하지 않는다. D는 '패턴 제시'라는 틀은 맞지만 결론이 정반대로, 지문은 거리만이 원인이 아니라고 말한다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence describes a pattern: stock routes were denser where leases were shortest, and longer tenures brought more on-station infrastructure. That pattern backs Marchetti's claim that land policy shaped how meat reached cities, so B is correct. A is wrong because the historians' view appears in the first sentence, and the underlined sentence is Marchetti's evidence, not that view. C is wrong because the sentence before it gives the reasoning about incentives, and the underlined sentence says nothing about what drovers preferred. D describes the sentence's form correctly (it offers a pattern) but gets the conclusion backward, since the text says droving was not simply a response to distance.

quality.seed: economics and business — Australian cattle station pastoral lease system and long-distance droving networks supplying colonial urban meat demand

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 짧은 임차 지역에 가축 이동로가 많고 긴 임차 지역에 현지 시설이 많다는 상관 패턴을 제시하며, 이는 '임대 정책이 육류 유통 방식을 형성했다'는 Marchetti 주장의 근거로 기능하므로 B가 정답임을 직접 확인. A(역사가 견해는 첫 문장), C(유인 설명은 직전 문장이며 드로버 선호를 다루지 않음), D(결론이 정반대)는 모두 지문 근거로 배제 가능. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 B 결론과 선택지 참조가 일치하고 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 가상의 역사가·일반적 역사 배경으로 저작권·사실 오류 우려 없음. 패턴 식별 + 주장과의 연결이라는 두 단계 판단이 필요하고 C·D가 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: B가 명확한 정답. A는 첫 문장의 역사가 견해를 이용한 함정이고, C는 앞 문장의 인과를 이용한 함정이며, D는 형식은 맞지만 결론이 반대인 함정이다. 오답이 부분적 근거를 가지므로 medium 난이도에 적합하다. 다만 A는 Marchetti가 기존 견해를 '거부'하지 않고 '또한(also)'으로 보완한다는 점에서 배제가 비교적 쉽다.

problem.passage:
Tardigrades, microscopic animals often called water bears, can survive almost complete drying by entering a state known as anhydrobiosis. As water leaves their bodies, they pull in their legs and contract into a compact form called a tun, and their metabolism slows to levels that can barely be detected. For years, researchers assumed that tardigrades, like brine shrimp and some nematodes, protected their cells mainly by filling them with the sugar trehalose, which turns into a glassy solid that holds delicate structures in place. However, many tardigrade species produce little or no trehalose. In 2017, biologist Thomas Boothby and colleagues reported that tardigrades instead rely on a family of proteins found only in their group, called tardigrade-specific intrinsically disordered proteins (TDPs). When genes for these proteins were silenced, the animals no longer survived drying well, and when the proteins were added to yeast and bacteria, those organisms became more tolerant of desiccation. Like trehalose, the proteins appear to form a glass-like matrix as cells dry, which suggests that tardigrades arrived at a familiar protective strategy by using a very different molecule.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
problem.stimulus: Tardigrades, microscopic animals often called water bears, can survive almost complete drying by entering a state known as anhydrobiosis. As water leaves their bodies, they pull in their legs and contract into a compact form called a tun, and their metabolism slows to levels that can barely be detected. For years, researchers assumed that tardigrades, like brine shrimp and some nematodes, protected their cells mainly by filling them with the sugar trehalose, which turns into a glassy solid that holds delicate structures in place. However, many tardigrade species produce little or no trehalose. In 2017, biologist Thomas Boothby and colleagues reported that tardigrades instead rely on a family of proteins found only in their group, called tardigrade-specific intrinsically disordered proteins (TDPs). When genes for these proteins were silenced, the animals no longer survived drying well, and when the proteins were added to yeast and bacteria, those organisms became more tolerant of desiccation. Like trehalose, the proteins appear to form a glass-like matrix as cells dry, which suggests that tardigrades arrived at a familiar protective strategy by using a very different molecule.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Tardigrades survive drying mainly by contracting into a tun and slowing their metabolism, which makes the chemical makeup of their cells less important than researchers once believed.
Tardigrades protect their cells during drying by producing larger amounts of trehalose than brine shrimp and nematodes do, which explains why they tolerate harsher conditions.
Tardigrades appear to protect their cells during drying with proteins unique to their group, which seem to work much as trehalose does in other animals.
Tardigrade proteins have been shown to make yeast and bacteria more tolerant of drying, which suggests the proteins may soon be widely used to preserve other organisms.
problem.explanation: 이 지문은 트레할로스가 주된 보호 수단이라는 기존 가정을 소개한 뒤, 타디그레이드는 고유 단백질(TDP)에 의존하며 이 단백질이 트레할로스처럼 유리 같은 기질을 만든다는 점을 제시하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 툰 형성과 대사 저하라는 지문의 세부 내용을 다루지만, 화학적 보호가 덜 중요하다는 주장은 지문에 없다. B는 트레할로스를 언급하지만, 지문은 많은 종이 트레할로스를 거의 만들지 않는다고 말하므로 지문과 모순된다. D는 효모·세균 실험이라는 근거 하나만 보고 지문에 없는 미래 응용까지 추론한 것이다.
problem.explanationEn: C is correct. The passage first describes the old assumption that trehalose was the main protection, then reports that tardigrades rely on their own unique proteins (TDPs), which seem to form a glassy matrix the same way trehalose does. A uses real details from the passage, the tun and the slowed metabolism, but the passage never says that cell chemistry matters less. B mentions trehalose, but it contradicts the passage, which says many species make little or no trehalose. D takes one supporting detail, the yeast and bacteria experiment, and adds a prediction about future uses that the passage never makes.

quality.seed: life science — Tardigrades' cryptobiosis mechanism and anhydrobiosis survival strategy enabling extreme environmental stress tolerance

hardJudge.note: 지문은 Boothby et al. 2017(Molecular Cell)의 TDP 연구를 정확히 반영함(RNAi 침묵 시 생존율 저하, 효모·세균 발현 시 내건성 증가, 유리화). 정답 C는 '기존 가정(트레할로스) → 새로운 발견(고유 단백질) → 유사한 보호 전략'이라는 지문 구조를 정확히 요약. A는 실제 세부(툰·대사 저하)를 쓰되 지문에 없는 주장을 덧붙였고, D는 실험 세부를 근거로 지문 밖 응용을 추론해 둘 다 비교·배제가 필요한 오답. B는 지문과 직접 모순되지만 트레할로스 언급으로 표면상 그럴듯함. 한·영 해설 모두 글자 참조와 논리가 일치하며 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 오리지널 작성 지문으로 보이며 저작권 의심 없음.

advisory.note: Boothby et al. 2017 실제 연구와 부합. 오답 A·D는 지문 세부를 부분적으로 활용해 비교가 필요하고, B는 명백한 모순이지만 그럴듯함. medium 적합.

problem.passage:
Many mammals, from rats to rhesus monkeys, eat the placenta shortly after giving birth, a behavior known as placentophagy. A long-standing explanation holds that the placenta replenishes iron and protein lost during delivery. Yet biologist Mark Kristal and colleagues observed that rats fed placenta did not show meaningfully better nutrient levels than rats fed ordinary meat of equal weight. What the placenta-fed rats did show was a stronger natural pain-relieving response during and after birth, an effect that ordinary meat did not produce. Kristal's team traced this effect to a substance in placental tissue and amniotic fluid that appears to amplify the body's own opioid system. Building on such findings, some researchers now suspect that placentophagy is valuable less as a meal than as a source of chemical signals, possibly including ones that influence oxytocin release and early maternal care, though this link has not yet been firmly established.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
problem.stimulus: Many mammals, from rats to rhesus monkeys, eat the placenta shortly after giving birth, a behavior known as placentophagy. A long-standing explanation holds that the placenta replenishes iron and protein lost during delivery. Yet biologist Mark Kristal and colleagues observed that rats fed placenta did not show meaningfully better nutrient levels than rats fed ordinary meat of equal weight. What the placenta-fed rats did show was a stronger natural pain-relieving response during and after birth, an effect that ordinary meat did not produce. Kristal's team traced this effect to a substance in placental tissue and amniotic fluid that appears to amplify the body's own opioid system. Building on such findings, some researchers now suspect that placentophagy is valuable less as a meal than as a source of chemical signals, possibly including ones that influence oxytocin release and early maternal care, though this link has not yet been firmly established.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Evidence from rats suggests that eating the placenta may benefit mammal mothers mainly through its biochemical effects rather than its nutritional value.
Evidence from rats suggests that eating the placenta benefits mammal mothers mainly by restoring the iron and protein lost during birth.
Evidence from rats suggests that eating the placenta triggers oxytocin release that directly strengthens early maternal care in mammals.
Evidence from rats suggests that eating the placenta offers mammal mothers no measurable advantage over eating ordinary meat.
problem.explanation: 이 글은 영양 회복 가설이 쥐 실험 결과로 약해졌고, 진통 효과와 화학 신호가 더 중요한 이점일 수 있다고 말하므로 정답은 A이다. B는 글에서 소개만 하고 반박하는 기존 가설을 그대로 주장한다. C는 글 마지막에 나오지만 아직 확인되지 않았다고 밝힌 옥시토신 연결을 확정된 사실처럼 말한다. D는 영양 면에서는 맞지만, 일반 고기에는 없던 진통 효과를 무시한다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says the rat findings weakened the nutrient-recovery hypothesis and points instead to pain relief and chemical signals as the likely benefits, so A is correct. B states the older hypothesis, which the text brings up only so it can challenge it. C treats the oxytocin link as fact, but the text says that link has not yet been firmly established. D holds up only for nutrition, since it ignores the pain-relieving effect that ordinary meat did not produce.

hardJudge.note: 정답 A 검산 일치: 글은 영양 가설(B)을 소개 후 쥐 실험으로 약화시키고, 진통 효과·화학 신호를 핵심 이점으로 제시하며, 옥시토신 연결은 미확정이라고 명시(C 배제). D는 영양 비교에서만 맞고 진통 효과를 무시하여 부분 정답형 오답으로 기능. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 글자 참조와 결론이 일치하고 자연스러움. problem.passage:
Three-toed sloths descend from the forest canopy about once a week to defecate at the base of their trees, a trip that exposes them to predators and burns precious energy. Ecologist Jonathan Pauli and colleagues proposed that the habit is tied to moths living in the sloths' fur: female moths leave the sloth during these descents to lay eggs in the dung, and the emerging adults fly up to colonize sloths in the canopy. The moths, in turn, appear to deposit nitrogen and other nutrients into the fur, fueling the growth of algae there. __Notably, the researchers found that sloths carrying more moths also had higher concentrations of inorganic nitrogen and greater algal biomass in their fur.__ Because sloths have been observed licking algae from their coats, and because the algae are rich in digestible carbohydrates and lipids, the team suggested that this greenish growth may supplement the sloths' notoriously low-nutrient diet of leaves, in addition to helping camouflage them among the foliage.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a finding that challenges the claim that sloths descend from the canopy in order to aid the moths' reproduction.
It provides evidence for a proposed link between the moths and algal growth that the text goes on to connect to a possible benefit for sloths.
It introduces a finding that explains why sloths choose to defecate at the base of their trees rather than in the canopy.
It offers an observation suggesting that algae, rather than moths, are the main source of nitrogen in sloths' fur.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 나방이 많을수록 털 속 질소와 조류가 많다는 결과로, 바로 앞 문장의 '나방이 영양분을 공급해 조류 성장을 돕는다'는 주장을 뒷받침하고, 이후 문장은 이 조류가 나무늘보의 영양·위장에 도움이 될 수 있다고 연결하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 이 결과가 연구진의 가설을 반박하는 것이 아니라 오히려 지지한다는 점에서 틀렸다. C는 나무늘보의 하강 행동이 지문에서 다뤄지긴 하지만, 밑줄 문장은 하강의 이유가 아니라 털 속 성분을 다룬다. D는 질소의 원천을 거꾸로 서술하고 있는데, 지문은 나방이 영양분을 공급한다고 말한다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence reports that sloths with more moths had more nitrogen and algae in their fur. This backs up the previous sentence's claim that moths supply nutrients that help algae grow, and the next sentence then ties those algae to possible nutrition and camouflage benefits for sloths, so B is correct. A is wrong because the finding supports the researchers' hypothesis instead of challenging it. C is wrong because the text does discuss the descents, but the underlined sentence is about what is in the fur, not about why sloths come down to defecate. D reverses the source of the nitrogen, since the text says the moths supply the nutrients.

problem.passage:
Remoras are fish that ride on sharks, whales, and sea turtles, clinging to their hosts with a flattened disc on top of the head. The disc is a modified dorsal fin whose rows of bony plates, called lamellae, can be raised to create pockets of low pressure against the host's skin. For decades, researchers assumed that remoras attached wherever they could grip and simply endured the turbulent water rushing past. __However, when biologist Brooke Flammang and colleagues attached tags to blue whales and filmed the remoras riding on them, they found that the fish gathered mostly in a few areas, such as behind the blowhole, where the flow of water over the whale's body is slower.__ In these sheltered zones, a remora experiences far less drag than it would in open water, letting it hitch a ride while spending little energy, and its disc lets it slide across the skin to feed without fully letting go.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

options: It explains how the lamellae on a remora's disc produce the low pressure that holds the fish against a host.
It presents evidence that remoras on blue whales face stronger turbulence than researchers had previously estimated.

B borrows the word turbulence, yet the finding shows remoras avoid strong flow rather than face more of it. D correctly treats the sentence as a finding, but the text never mentions a debate about preferred host species.

problem.passage:
Satellite images taken since the 1960s show that the open water of Lake Chad, on the southern edge of the Sahara, shrank by roughly 90 percent within a few decades. The shrinkage was often presented as a textbook case of climate-driven desertification across the Sahel. More recent analyses that combine satellite gravity measurements with long-term rainfall records make the picture more complicated. These studies find that the lake's northern basin did largely dry out during the severe droughts of the 1970s and 1980s, but that the southern basin has been fairly stable since the 1990s, and groundwater beneath the region has even increased slightly. Researchers argue that the lake's decline reflects a shift in rainfall patterns followed by partial recovery, along with heavy irrigation withdrawals, rather than a steady, ongoing march of the desert.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

The shrinkage was often presented as a textbook case of climate-driven desertification across the Sahel. More recent analyses that combine satellite gravity measurements with long-term rainfall records make the picture more complicated. These studies find that the lake's northern basin did largely dry out during the severe droughts of the 1970s and 1980s, but that the southern basin has been fairly stable since the 1990s, and groundwater beneath the region has even increased slightly. Researchers argue that the lake's decline reflects a shift in rainfall patterns followed by partial recovery, along with heavy irrigation withdrawals, rather than a steady, ongoing march of the desert.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Satellite images confirm that Lake Chad has lost about 90 percent of its water, showing that desertification across the Sahel continues to speed up.
Newer data suggest that Lake Chad's decline came mostly from past droughts and water use and has partly leveled off, not from continuous desertification.

Groundwater beneath the Lake Chad region has increased enough that the lake's open water is expected to return to its 1960s extent.
problem.explanation: 이 글은 처음에는 차드호 축소를 기후로 인한 사막화의 대표 사례로 소개한 뒤, 새로운 자료가 그런 시각을 수정한다고 설명한다. 축소의 원인은 과거의 가뭄과 관개였고 이후 어느 정도 안정되었다는 것이 핵심이므로 B가 정답이다. A는 90% 감소라는 수치는 맞지만, 글이 반박하는 '계속되는 사막화' 해석을 그대로 받아들이고 있다. C는 관개가 언급되었다는 점은 맞지만, 강우 변화를 원인에서 빼고 '유일한 원인'이라고 지나치게 단정한다. D는 지하수 증가라는 세부 내용을 1960년대 수준으로의 회복 예측으로 부풀렸는데, 글에는 그런 예측이 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The text first presents Lake Chad's shrinkage as the classic example of climate-driven desertification, then explains how newer data revise that view. Its main point is that the decline came from past droughts and irrigation and has partly stabilized, so B is correct. A gets the 90 percent figure right, but it accepts the "ongoing desertification" interpretation that the text argues against. C is right that irrigation is mentioned, but it leaves out the shift in rainfall and goes too far by calling irrigation the only cause. D takes the detail about rising groundwater and stretches it into a prediction that the lake will return to its 1960s size, which the text never makes.

problem.passage:
On most days, air near the ground is warmer than the air above it, so pollutants released by cars and furnaces rise and disperse as the warm air lifts. During winter in mountain valleys such as Utah's Salt Lake Valley, however, cold, dense air can settle on the valley floor beneath a layer of warmer air that has moved in overhead. This arrangement, called a thermal inversion, acts like a lid: the cold surface air cannot rise through the warmer layer, and the surrounding mountains block it from flowing out sideways. Researchers tracking fine-particle pollution in the valley have found that daily emissions during inversion episodes are roughly the same as on clear days. Yet particle concentrations climb steadily the longer an inversion persists, sometimes exceeding federal health limits within a few days, and then drop sharply once a passing storm mixes the layers apart.

Based on the text, what accounts for the worsening air quality in the Salt Lake Valley during inversion episodes?

This arrangement, called a thermal inversion, acts like a lid: the cold surface air cannot rise through the warmer layer, and the surrounding mountains block it from flowing out sideways. Researchers tracking fine-particle pollution in the valley have found that daily emissions during inversion episodes are roughly the same as on clear days. Warm air arriving overhead carries pollutants into the valley from distant sources beyond the mountains.
Pollutants that would ordinarily disperse accumulate because the cold surface air is held in place by the warm layer and the mountains.
Storms passing through the valley stir up particles that then remain suspended near the ground for several days.
problem.explanation: 지문은 역전 기간에도 배출량은 맑은 날과 비슷하지만, 따뜻한 상층이 뚜껑처럼 작용하고 산이 옆으로 빠져나가는 것을 막아 오염물질이 쌓인다고 설명하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 겨울철 연소와 그럴듯하게 연결되지만 배출량이 거의 같다는 진술과 모순된다. B는 따뜻한 공기가 위로 들어온다는 점은 맞지만, 그 공기가 오염물질을 실어 온다는 내용은 지문에 없다. D는 폭풍을 언급하지만 지문에서 폭풍은 층을 섞어 농도를 낮추는 역할을 한다.
problem.explanationEn: C is correct. The text says emissions during inversions are about the same as on clear days, but the warm layer acts as a lid and the mountains block sideways flow, so pollutants build up. A sounds reasonable because furnaces burn more in winter, but it contradicts the statement that emissions stay roughly the same. B is right that warm air moves in overhead, but the text never says that air brings pollution with it. D mentions storms, but in the text storms mix the layers apart and lower concentrations.

problem.passage:
In a handful of estuaries worldwide, such as the Qiantang in China and the Severn in Britain, the incoming tide arrives not as a gradual rise but as a single wall of water called a tidal bore. Researchers have long attributed bores mainly to the funnel shape of these estuaries: as the channel narrows and shallows upstream, the energy of the tidal wave is squeezed into a smaller cross section, steepening its front. __Yet funneling alone cannot explain why some narrow estuaries produce towering bores while others of similar shape produce none.__ Hydrologists now argue that resonance is also crucial. When the time a tidal wave takes to travel the length of an estuary and reflect back roughly matches a fraction of the tidal period, successive waves reinforce one another, amplifying the tidal range enough for a bore to form.

Most tsunamis are generated when an undersea earthquake abruptly lifts or drops a section of seafloor, displacing the water column above it. problem.passage:
When a liquid is blasted with intense sound waves, tiny gas bubbles form, swell, and then collapse violently, a process called acoustic cavitation. In 1990, physicist Felipe Gaitan found a way to trap a single bubble at the center of a flask of water, where it expanded and collapsed tens of thousands of times per second, giving off a faint flash of blue light with every collapse. This effect, known as sonoluminescence, had been seen in clouds of bubbles since the 1930s, but isolating one bubble let researchers measure it precisely. They found that each flash lasts less than a billionth of a second and that the gas inside the bubble may reach thousands of degrees as the bubble shrinks. Still, how the light is actually produced is debated. Some researchers credit heating from shock waves converging inside the bubble, while others argue that the hot gas simply glows the way any very hot material does, and so far no experiment has clearly ruled out either explanation.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

problem.passage:
Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are crystalline materials built from metal clusters linked by organic molecules, forming networks riddled with tiny pores. Because chemists can choose the linkers, they long assumed that making pores as large and numerous as possible would yield the best materials for capturing gases such as carbon dioxide from industrial exhaust. Some MOFs do have enormous internal surface areas: a single gram can contain more surface than a soccer field. Yet chemist Omar Farha and colleagues found that several of the highest-surface-area frameworks performed poorly at pulling carbon dioxide out of mixtures that also contained nitrogen. In those wide pores, both gases drifted in and out with little preference.

The more successful frameworks in the team's tests had narrower pores lined with chemical groups that interact strongly with carbon dioxide molecules but only weakly with nitrogen. Shrinking pores reduced the total amount of gas a material could hold, but it greatly increased how selectively the material held carbon dioxide. For separation tasks, the researchers concluded, tailoring pore size and chemistry to the target molecule matters more than maximizing open space.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

problem.passage:
Photochromic eyeglass lenses darken outdoors and clear indoors because of molecules embedded in their plastic. In many lenses, these are spirooxazine molecules, which normally hold a folded, colorless shape. When ultraviolet light strikes one, a chemical bond breaks and the molecule unfolds into a flat form that absorbs visible light, tinting the lens. __Yet the flat form is not stable on its own: once ultraviolet exposure stops, heat from the surroundings gradually pushes the molecules back into their folded shape.__ This reversal is why wearers notice that their lenses fade more slowly on a cold day than on a warm one, since lower temperatures supply less of the energy needed to refold the molecules.

problem.passage:
In petroleum refining, catalytic cracking breaks long hydrocarbon chains into the smaller molecules that make up gasoline. Many refineries rely on zeolites, crystalline aluminosilicates riddled with pores less than a nanometer wide, to speed this process. Because reactions occur mainly inside these micropores, the pore dimensions determine which molecules can enter, which transition states can form, and which products can escape. __One might therefore expect that the zeolite with the widest pores would always be preferred, since it admits the greatest variety of feedstock molecules.__ Yet engineers often favor zeolites with narrower channels: by excluding bulky branched molecules and preventing the formation of large intermediates that tend to produce coke, these tighter pores yield a more predictable product mixture and extend the catalyst's working life.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

It presents a finding that the text then uses to explain how coke forms inside zeolites.

B는 코크 형성이 뒤에 언급되기는 하지만 밑줄 문장은 연구 결과가 아니라 가정이며 코크 설명의 근거로 쓰이지 않는다. C는 촉매 수명이 뒤에 나오지만 그것은 밑줄 문장을 뒷받침하는 것이 아니라 반박한다. D는 밑줄 문장이 정의가 아니고, 글은 원료 선택이 아니라 촉매 선택을 다룬다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence begins with "One might therefore expect," which offers a prediction that seems to follow from the earlier point about pore size: the widest pores should always be best. The next sentence opens with "Yet" and explains why narrower pores are often chosen, which shows that the expectation is incomplete. That makes A the answer. B doesn't work because the sentence is an assumption, not a finding, and it isn't used to explain how coke forms, even though coke comes up later. C doesn't work because the point about catalyst lifespan argues against the underlined sentence instead of supporting it. D doesn't work because the sentence isn't a definition, and the text is about choosing a catalyst, not choosing feedstocks.

problem.stimulus: When a suspension of identical silica microspheres is left to settle slowly, the particles can arrange themselves into a highly ordered lattice without any external guidance. sensitive

problem.explanation: 콜론 뒤 내용은 크기가 다른 입자가 조금만 섞여도 배열이 무너진다는 점, 즉 공정이 작은 변화에 쉽게 영향을 받는다는 것을 설명하므로 B(sensitive)가 정답이다. A(spontaneous)는 첫 문장의 '외부 유도 없이'와 맞아 보이지만 콜론 뒤의 결함 설명을 뒷받침하지 못한다. C(efficient)는 질서 있는 격자 형성과 연결될 듯하나 지문은 효율이 아닌 취약성을 강조한다. D(reversible)는 침강·배열 과정과 그럴듯하게 어울리지만 되돌릴 수 있다는 내용은 지문에 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The text after the colon explains that even a few spheres of a different size disrupt the packing, so the process is easily affected by small variations, which makes B ("sensitive") correct. A ("spontaneous") seems to fit the first sentence's "without any external guidance," but it doesn't set up the explanation about defects that follows the colon. C ("efficient") might seem to go with forming an ordered lattice, but the text stresses how fragile the process is, not how efficient it is. D ("reversible") sounds plausible for a settling process, but nothing in the text says the arrangement can be undone.

problem.explanation: 지문은 균열이 "무작위 지점에서 시작되지 않고" 결정립 경계에서 생기며 "나중에야" 접합부 전체로 퍼진다고 말하므로, 빈칸에는 '시작되다'라는 뜻의 C(originate)가 들어가야 한다. A(propagate)는 균열과 자주 쓰이는 단어지만 '퍼지다'라는 뜻이어서, 퍼짐을 나중 단계로 따로 언급한 문장과 맞지 않는다. D(accumulate)는 같은 위치에 변형률이 쌓인다는 내용과 비슷해 보이지만, 쌓이는 것은 변형률이지 균열 자체가 아니다. B(terminate)는 균열이 '끝난다'는 뜻이라 '시작'을 대비시키는 문맥과 반대된다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says cracks "rarely begin at random points" and form at grain boundaries, and that they "only later spread," so the blank has to mean "start." That makes C (originate) the answer. A (propagate) is a common word for cracks, but it means "spread," and the text saves spreading for the later stage. D (accumulate) sounds right because strain builds up at those boundaries, but strain is what accumulates there, not the cracks. B (terminate) means "end," which is the opposite of the idea of where cracks begin.

B connects to the fluid stiffening into a near-solid, but the passage stresses "any level," not just the highest one. C might suggest the resistance disappearing, but "concealed" means hidden, which doesn't fit the context.

problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 "chemists ... published ... the WLF equation"이라는 독립절에 긴 동격어구가 붙은 형태이고, 빈칸 뒤 "by applying it, engineers can stitch..."도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결해야 하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이은 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이다. B는 문장부호 없이 이어 붙인 비문이며, "by applying"이 앞의 "degrees"를 수식하는 것처럼 잘못 읽힌다. C는 관계사 which를 넣어 종속절처럼 보이게 했지만, 절 안에 이미 "it"이 있어 which가 맡을 문법적 역할이 없으므로 비문이 된다.
problem.explanationEn: Before the blank you have an independent clause ("chemists ... published ... the WLF equation") followed by a long appositive. After the blank comes another full independent clause, "by applying it, engineers can stitch...," which has its own subject and verb. Two independent clauses can be joined by a semicolon, so D is correct. A joins them with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B runs the clauses together with no punctuation and makes "by applying" seem to modify "degrees." C adds "which" to make the second part look like a relative clause, but the clause already contains "it," so "which" has no grammatical role and the sentence breaks down.

problem.passage:
Electrospinning is a method for drawing polymer solutions into fibers far thinner than a human hair. A droplet of solution sits at the tip of a needle, and when a high voltage is applied, electric charge builds up on the droplet's surface until it stretches into a cone and ejects a thin jet toward a grounded collector. Engineers once assumed that the final fiber diameter depended mainly on how viscous the solution was. Work by materials scientist Elena Varga and colleagues suggests a more complicated picture: as the jet travels, charges on its surface repel one another and cause the jet to whip in rapid loops, stretching it far more than a straight path would. By adjusting the shape of the electric field between needle and collector, Varga's team was able to lengthen this whipping phase and produce fibers less than half as thick as those made from the same solution under a standard setup.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

A only restates the opening description of the process and misses the study's central finding. B overstates the text: it calls the picture "more complicated" but never says viscosity has no effect. D credits increased voltage, but the team changed the shape of the electric field, not the voltage level.

problem.passage:
Thermoelectric modules convert heat directly into electricity through the Seebeck effect: when one side of a semiconductor junction is hotter than the other, charge carriers drift toward the cooler side, producing a voltage. Because the devices have no moving parts, engineers have long hoped to attach them to car exhausts and factory chimneys to recover energy that would otherwise be lost. __Yet the very materials that conduct electricity well tend to conduct heat well too, so the temperature difference the module depends on quickly evens out.__ For this reason, most commercial modules convert less than ten percent of the heat passing through them. Researchers at several laboratories are now designing semiconductors laced with nanoscale grain boundaries that scatter heat-carrying vibrations while letting electrons pass, an approach that could loosen this trade-off.
